title: Prospective comparison of CT- and MRI-based tumor delineation based on intraoperative navigation and spatially annotated pathology in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma.
abstract: Introduction Precise tumor delineation is critical for navigation-guided surgery and radiotherapy (RT) in locally advanced midfacial squamous cell carcinoma (SCC). Contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT) and magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) are both recommended for staging and provide complementary information. However, quantitative comparisons of CT- and MRI-based tumor contours remain scarce, while a spatial comparison with histopathological data has never been performed. Therefore, we prospectively compared gross tumor volumes (GTV) derived from CT and MRI before navigation-guided surgery and correlated the results with spatially annotated pathology. Methods This imaging sub-analysis was conducted within the prospective NAVIGATORR trial (NCT05671458). Fifteen patients with locally advanced midfacial SCC underwent contrast-enhanced CT and 1.5T or 3T MRI (T1w, T2w, DWI) for navigation-based surgery planning. Datasets were rigidly co-registered and an experienced radiologist independently contoured the GTV on CT and MRI while blinded to the other modality. Besides qualitative and volumetric evaluation, spatial agreement was assessed using the Dice similarity coefficient (DSC) and Hausdorff distance (HD). Tumor contours were correlated with spatially annotated intraoperative biopsy locations and histopathological results. Results Fifteen patients and 109 spatially annotated biopsy locations (19 tumor-positive) were analyzed. MRI was preferred for tumor delineation by the radiologist in all cases, with superior differentiation between tumor and mucosal swelling (73%) and improved soft tissue contrast (67%). MRI based GTVs were significantly larger than CT-based GTVs (median 28.3 ml vs. 16.8 ml; p = 0.02). DSC values demonstrated fair agreement with considerable heterogeneity (median 0.58; IQR 0.47-0.65), and median HD was 16 mm (IQR 12-27 mm). MRI-based contours encompassed numerically more tumor-positive biopsy locations than CT-based contours (6/19 vs. 1/19; clustered McNemar p = 0.20) while including fewer tumor-negative locations (7/90 vs. 10/90; p = 0.53). At patient level, at least one tumor-positive biopsy was located inside the contour in 3/8 (MRI) vs. 1/8 (CT) patients. Discussion GTV delineation differs substantially between MRI and CT in locally advanced midfacial SCC, and the two modalities provide complementary information. These exploratory findings support the complementary use of MRI and CT for tumor visualization. Clinical implications remain to be shown by the primary endpoint analysis of the NAVIGATORR trial.

title: Optical coherence tomography for surgical margin assessment of soft-tissue sarcomas of the extremities and trunk.
abstract: Introduction Incomplete resection of superficial trunk and extremity soft-tissue sarcomas can impact the risk of local recurrence and overall prognosis for patients after surgical resection. Multiple methods have been described for intraoperative surgical margin assessment of soft-tissue sarcomas, including optical coherence tomography (OCT) evaluation of surgical margins. The accuracy of OCT imaging for evaluating the surgical margins of soft-tissue sarcoma has not been reported. The first aim of this study was to determine the OCT imaging features of different tissue types at the surgical margins when compared to histopathology to allow for image interpretation training for observers. The second aim was to determine the diagnostic accuracy of OCT for identification of incomplete margin status for soft-tissue sarcomas of the superficial trunk or extremities. Methods The surgical margins of 20 soft-tissue sarcoma specimens were imaged using OCT following surgical resection. The OCT images from the first five tumors were used to identify features of different tissue types compared to histopathology and create a training presentation. The OCT images from all tumors were then used to create a training set and test set. Seven observers underwent a training session using a training presentation and interpreted a training and test set. Images were graded on a numeric scale from 1 (no tumor present) to 4 (tumor present). The results of the test set were used to evaluate the sensitivity, specificity, accuracy, and inter- and intraobserver variability. Results The overall sensitivity and specificity for detection of tumor on the surgical margin were 83.5% [95% confidence interval (CI): 74.6% -89.7%] and 76.8% (95% CI: 68.2% -83.6%), respectively. The overall correct classification rate of the surgical margin was 162/203 (79.8%; 95% CI: 73.8% -84.7%). Discussion Further research is needed in an intraoperative setting with a larger patient population to evaluate the use of OCT to evaluate the surgical margins for soft-tissue sarcomas.

title: Dosimetry-guided morphomic modeling using daily FBCT for automated all-in-one radiotherapy eligibility assessment in postoperative cervical cancer.
abstract: Objective This study aimed to develop an automated decision-making model based on daily fan-beam CT (FBCT) morphomic features to determine whether a treatment fraction is suitable for AIO-RT initiation. Methods A total of 48 postoperative cervical cancer patients with 313 FBCT fractions were retrospectively analyzed. Morphomic features were extracted from bladder, rectum, intrarectal gas, bilateral femoral head, and inter-organ spatial relationships. Feature selection was performed using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO), and predictive models were built using Random Forest (RF) and Gradient Boosting Machine (GBM) under leave-one-patient-out cross-validation. Results Both models achieved consistent discriminative performance (AUC = 0.958 for RF and 0.952 for GBM). Bladder-related morphological features were the dominant predictors, particularly bladder volume and shape-derived descriptors. Spatial features also contributed to classification performance, while rectal gas showed limited but complementary predictive value. Conclusion The proposed FBCT-based morphomic framework can accurately identify unsuitable fractions for AIO-RT before workflow initiation, providing a practical and interpretable decision-support tool for adaptive radiotherapy workflow optimization.

title: Breast cancer metastasis to the thyroid gland: case report.
abstract: Background Distant metastasis is common in highly malignant tumors. However, metastasis to the thyroid gland from extrathyroidal malignancies is extremely rare. Among primary tumors metastasizing to the thyroid, renal cell carcinoma, lung cancer, and head and neck cancer are most frequently reported. Breast cancer, despite its high prevalence, accounts for a disproportionately small fraction of thyroid metastases. Here we present the clinical course of a patient with a history of invasive ductal carcinoma(IDC) who was subsequently found to have thyroid metastasis. Case presentation A 53-year-old female patient had a history of IDC of the breast 10 years ago. She underwent total thyroidectomy due to thyroid nodules with high suspicion of malignancy on PET-CT. Postoperative pathology combined with immunohistochemistry (IHC) confirmed metastasis of breast cancer to the thyroid. Despite receiving endocrine therapy and chemotherapy after surgery, the disease continued to progress, resulting in a poor prognosis. Conclusion Metastases to the thyroid and supraclavicular lymph nodes developing in a patient more than a decade after breast cancer diagnosis present a major diagnostic challenge. A combination of IHC and comprehensive imaging is essential for accurate diagnosis. Understanding the underlying metastatic mechanisms may aid in optimizing surveillance and treatment strategies.

title: Salivary glands auto-segmentation in head and neck radiotherapy: imaging modalities, models, and clinical relevance.
abstract: Radiotherapy-induced salivary gland injury is a major contributor to xerostomia and impaired quality of life in patients with head and neck cancer, making accurate organ-at-risk delineation clinically important. Deep learning-based auto-segmentation has the potential to improve contouring efficiency and consistency, but reported performance is heterogeneous and its clinical significance is not always clear. This narrative review summarizes current evidence on salivary gland auto-segmentation across computed tomography (CT), magnetic resonance imaging (MRI), and prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography-computed tomography (PSMA PET-CT), with particular emphasis on gland-specific challenges, performance evaluation, and clinical translation. CT has the largest evidence base and remains most relevant to routine radiotherapy planning, whereas MRI provides improved soft-tissue visualization and PSMA PET-CT offers high functional contrast for selected salivary structures. Across modalities, segmentation performance is generally more challenging for smaller structures, particularly the sublingual and tubarial gland regions. Importantly, geometric metrics such as the Dice similarity coefficient do not alone establish clinical acceptability or dosimetric equivalence; evaluation should also consider boundary accuracy, expert correction burden, clinical acceptability, and dosimetric impact. Current evidence is further limited by heterogeneous study designs and reference standards, scarce external validation, and limited evidence linking auto-segmentation directly to treatment-related toxicity or patient outcomes. Future research should prioritize multi-institutional validation, clinically meaningful evaluation, improved segmentation of small glands, and human-in-the-loop integration into adaptive radiotherapy. Overall, auto-segmentation represents a promising tool for salivary gland delineation, but its clinical implementation should be supported by evidence extending beyond geometric accuracy alone.

title: Pretreatment ET radiomics based on primary-tumor HR status for assessing the risk of local progression after GKRS in BCBM.
abstract: Background To determine whether hormone receptor (HR) status modifies the association between pretreatment enhancing-tumor (ET) MRI radiomics and 12-month lesion-level local progression after Gamma Knife radiosurgery (GKRS) for breast cancer brain metastases (BCBM). Methods We screened 61 patients and locked a cohort of 49 patients with 105 lesions, including 33 progressed and 72 non-progressed lesions. Enhancing tumor (ET) was manually delineated on pretreatment contrast-enhanced T1-weighted MRI. The prespecified model combined ET Rad-score, hormone receptor (HR) status and the ET Rad-score × HR interaction. Performance was evaluated using patient-grouped repeated nested cross-validation. Results The locked model achieved lesion-level ROC-AUC 0.750, average precision (AP) 0.567 and Brier score 0.204. Patient-balanced evaluation yielded ROC-AUC 0.786, AP 0.621 and Brier score 0.194. The ET Rad-score × HR interaction was positive in 98 of 100 outer folds. HR-positive lesions had higher ROC-AUC and AP and a lower Brier score (ROC-AUC 0.827, AP 0.664, Brier score 0.174). Patient-level maximum predicted risk achieved ROC-AUC 0.803 and AP 0.694. Descriptive median-risk stratification separated lesions with progression rates of 50.9% versus 11.5%. Conclusion Pretreatment ET radiomics showed an HR-dependent association with 12-month lesion-level local progression after GKRS in BCBM, supporting further investigation of HR-informed radiomic risk stratification. Public datasets provided construct support; endpoint-matched external validation is needed before clinical application.

title: Grade 3 cholestatic immune-related hepatitis under cemiplimab for high-risk locally advanced cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma: a case report from Germany.
abstract: Cutaneous squamous cell carcinoma (cSCC) is one of the most common types of skin cancer. While most cSCC are cured by surgery, those with high-risk features such as perineural invasion, infiltration of deep structures or bones, or incomplete resection carry a substantial risk of recurrence. Until recently, no systemic adjuvant treatment had demonstrated clinical benefit in terms of prolongation of relapse-free survival in this high-risk setting. The phase-3 randomized clinical trial C-POST demonstrated that adjuvant checkpoint immunotherapy with cemiplimab, a programmed cell death protein 1 (PD-1) inhibitor, prolongs disease-free survival after surgery and radiotherapy, thus leading to regulatory approval by the European Commission in 2025. We report the case of an 81-year-old male from Germany with type-2 diabetes and hypertension who presented with a rapidly enlarging cSCC of the right cheek. Histopathology showed a tumor thickness of 10.0 mm with infiltration of the subcutaneous tissue and mimetic muscles, perineural growth, and incomplete resection status. Imaging demonstrated involvement of the facial vein and infraorbital canal with bone destruction and maxillary sinus extension (pT3 cN0 cM0, stage III by AJCCv8). As complete resection was not feasible, definitive radiotherapy (60 Gy) was delivered to the residual tumor, followed by cemiplimab (350 mg every 3 weeks) with adjuvant intent, following the C-POST regimen. Treatment was complicated by grade 2 immune-related hepatitis with a cholestatic component that improved with oral corticosteroid therapy. However, the hepatitis recurred and, together with grade 3 fatigue, progressed to a grade 3 immune-related hepatitis with a predominantly cholestatic pattern, leading to hospital admission. Cross-sectional imaging and ultrasound excluded biliary obstruction and tumor relapse. Intravenous corticosteroids produced prompt biochemical improvement. Adjuvant cemiplimab was discontinued. This case illustrates the real-world translation of recently approved adjuvant immunotherapy to an elderly patient and highlights the recognition and management of a severe, cholestatic pattern of immune-related liver inflammation under anti-PD-1 checkpoint immunotherapy.

Imaging demonstrated involvement of the facial vein and infraorbital canal with bone destruction and maxillary sinus extension (pT3 cN0 cM0, stage III by AJCCv8). As complete resection was not feasible, definitive radiotherapy (60 Gy) was delivered to the residual tumor, followed by cemiplimab (350 mg every 3 weeks) with adjuvant intent, following the C-POST regimen. Treatment was complicated by grade 2 immune-related hepatitis with a cholestatic component that improved with oral corticosteroid therapy. However, the hepatitis recurred and, together with grade 3 fatigue, progressed to a grade 3 immune-related hepatitis with a predominantly cholestatic pattern, leading to hospital admission. Cross-sectional imaging and ultrasound excluded biliary obstruction and tumor relapse. Intravenous corticosteroids produced prompt biochemical improvement. Adjuvant cemiplimab was discontinued. This case illustrates the real-world translation of recently approved adjuvant immunotherapy to an elderly patient and highlights the recognition and management of a severe, cholestatic pattern of immune-related liver inflammation under anti-PD-1 checkpoint immunotherapy.

title: Pretreatment platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio and survival after definitive radio(chemo)therapy for head and neck squamous cell carcinoma: an exploratory cohort study.
abstract: Background Current staging provides limited prognostic accuracy in head and neck squamous cell carcinoma (HNSCC). We evaluated whether pretreatment systemic inflammatory ratios and 2-deoxy-2-[ 18 F]fluoro-D-glucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography ([ 18 F]FDG PET/CT) metabolic parameters are associated with survival in patients treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy. Methods We retrospectively studied 110 patients with HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy at a single center. Inflammatory ratios, including the platelet-to-lymphocyte ratio (PLR), were derived from a pretreatment blood count. Metabolic parameters were obtained from staging [ 18 F]FDG PET/CT. The primary endpoints were overall survival (OS) and disease-specific survival (DSS). A Cox model comprising PLR, p16 status, cT category and age was fitted for each endpoint. Missing p16 status was handled by multiple imputation. Results A higher PLR was independently associated with worse OS (HR per interquartile range 1.61, 95% CI 1.13-2.28; p = 0.008) and DSS (HR 1.78, 95% CI 1.21-2.60; p = 0.003), alongside p16-negativity. cT4 category and age were also independently associated with OS. p16 was missing in 30% of patients, mostly non-oropharyngeal tumors. Complete-case analysis was therefore restricted to 77 patients, in which the point estimates were similar, but the association no longer reached significance. PLR correlated weakly with cT category (Spearman ρ = 0.275, p = 0.004) without collinearity. In exploratory analyses, the association between a high PLR and worse survival was clear in oropharyngeal tumors but weaker in other subsites. Metabolic parameters did not demonstrate an independent association with survival after adjustment. Conclusions Pretreatment PLR was independently associated with worse OS and DSS in HNSCC treated with definitive radio(chemo)therapy in the primary multiple-imputation analysis. Effect estimates were consistent in direction and magnitude across all three approaches to missing p16 status. A higher PLR indicates a worse prognosis, but the association is modest and does not guide treatment selection. Prospective validation with prespecified cutoffs is required before clinical use.

title: Multiparametric MRI radiomics and clinical features for preoperative prediction of high-grade meningioma: a two-centre retrospective study.
abstract: Background Preoperative identification of high-grade meningioma remains challenging using clinical and conventional imaging features. We compared MRI radiomic and clinical models and assessed whether their integration improved external discrimination. Materials and methods This retrospective two-centre study included 284 patients, with 227 used for training and 57 for independent external testing. Radiomics from contrast-enhanced T1-weighted imaging (CE-T1WI), T2-weighted imaging (T2WI), and fluid-attenuated inversion recovery (FLAIR) underwent training-cohort screening, correlation filtering, and LASSO selection. The primary comparison assessed external area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) for joint-clinical versus clinical logistic regression (LR) models. Secondary comparisons assessed adding clinical predictors to joint imaging and combining sequences relative to T2WI. Bootstrap-based normal-approximation comparisons with paired resampling and Holm correction evaluated these three contrasts. Calibration, decision curves, and K-nearest neighbour (KNN) models were exploratory. Results The external cohort contained 48 low-grade and 9 high-grade tumours. All four imaging-only LR models had higher external bootstrap-mean AUC point estimates than the clinical model (0.663; 95% CI, 0.467-0.840). CE-T1WI yielded 0.863 (0.755-0.949), and FLAIR yielded 0.838 (0.724-0.932). T2WI and joint imaging yielded 0.719 (0.555-0.862) and 0.807 (0.640-0.941), respectively. The joint-clinical model had an external AUC of 0.754 (0.557-0.920). Imaging-only Brier scores (0.113-0.127) were lower than those of clinical (0.246) and joint-clinical (0.209) models. Both clinical and joint-clinical predictions overestimated risk in the external cohort. The primary joint-clinical versus clinical bootstrap-mean AUC difference was 0.091 (95% CI, -0.126 to 0.309; Holm-adjusted P = 0.410). None of the three planned contrasts remained significant after Holm correction. Conclusion MRI radiomics showed promising external discrimination and lower probability error than the clinical model in this cohort. These findings support further evaluation of radiomics for preoperative grade prediction, while the incremental benefit of clinical-radiomic integration remains unconfirmed.

title: EGFR-mutant lung adenocarcinoma with leptomeningeal metastasis after osimertinib treatment: intrathecal chemotherapy combined with targeted therapy supported by cerebrospinal fluid next generation sequencing - a case report.
abstract: Background Leptomeningeal metastasis (LM) is a severe complication of advanced non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC). Conventional cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) cytology has limited sensitivity and often delays diagnosis. We report a case of LM molecularly supported by CSF next-generation sequencing (NGS) after three negative cytological examinations. NGS also revealed a potential bypass resistance alteration that informed subsequent treatment considerations. Case A 57-year-old female never-smoker had EGFR exon 21 p.L858R-mutant lung adenocarcinoma. After 18 months of first-line osimertinib (80 mg once daily), she developed progressive nausea, vomiting, and dizziness. Contrast-enhanced cranial magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) showed linear leptomeningeal enhancement. Lumbar puncture showed markedly elevated intracranial pressure (>300 mmH2O) and increased CSF protein. However, three CSF cytological examinations (including cell block sections) found no malignant cells. CSF NGS detected the EGFR p.L858R mutation identical to the primary tumor, together with CDK4 amplification. Integrated with the clinical and MRI presentation, these findings supported a diagnosis of probable LM and suggested cell-cycle bypass activation as a potential mechanism associated with osimertinib resistance. After intrathecal methotrexate plus continued oral osimertinib, her neurological symptoms improved markedly, and intracranial pressure returned to normal. The first seizure occurred on March 19, 2026, and MRI on April 8, 2026 confirmed new brain parenchymal metastases. Whole-brain radiotherapy with a local boost to the metastases, antiepileptic treatment, and continued osimertinib led to obvious shrinkage of the intracranial lesions. Grade 3 thrombocytopenia and severe malnutrition occurred during multimodal therapy and improved with supportive care. At the last follow-up, the patient was clinically stable with an Eastern Cooperative Oncology Group performance status (ECOG PS) of 1. Conclusions CSF NGS can overcome the diagnostic bottleneck of cytology-negative LM. It can also identify potential resistance alterations and actionable targets (such as CDK4/6 inhibitors) at the same time, providing direction for subsequent targeted strategies. As part of multimodal therapy, intrathecal chemotherapy combined with an EGFR tyrosine kinase inhibitor (TKI) can contribute to disease control in the CSF compartment, whereas parenchymal progression still requires salvage radiotherapy. Cumulative hematological and nutritional toxicity should be monitored during sequential multimodal therapy.

title: Association between preoperative MRI-measured membranous urethral length and early urinary continence recovery after robot-assisted radical prostatectomy: a retrospective cohort study.
abstract: Background Robot-assisted radical prostatectomy (RARP) is a key surgical approach for localized prostate cancer, yet early postoperative urinary incontinence remains a major functional concern. Membranous urethral length (MUL), measurable by preoperative MRI, may predict continence recovery, but its relationship with early outcomes warrants further clarification. Objective To investigate the association between preoperative MRI-measured MUL and early complete urinary continence recovery after RARP, and to evaluate its dose-response relationship and discriminative ability. Methods This retrospective cohort study included 152 patients who underwent RARP (October 2024-March 2026). MUL was measured on preoperative T2-weighted MRI by two independent observers. Urinary continence (0 pads/day) was assessed at 1 and 3 months after catheter removal. Multivariable Logistic regression (1 month) and Firth penalized Logistic regression (3 months) were used. Restricted cubic spline, ROC curves, and propensity score matching were performed. Results Median MUL was 13.49 mm. Interobserver agreement was excellent (ICC = 0.946). Complete continence recovery rates at 1 and 3 months were 51.32% and 79.61%, respectively. Each 1-mm MUL increase was independently associated with higher odds of continence recovery at 1 month (OR = 1.758, 95% CI: 1.450-2.132, P<0.001) and 3 months (OR = 1.502, 95% CI: 1.247-1.809, P<0.001). Older age and higher BMI were associated with lower odds of 3-month recovery (both P<0.05). RCS analysis showed a linear dose-response relationship (P overall<0.001; P nonlinearity=0.540). MUL demonstrated moderate discriminative ability for 1-month (AUC = 0.822) and 3-month (AUC = 0.773) continence recovery. Conclusion Longer preoperative MUL was independently associated with higher likelihood of complete urinary continence recovery at 1 and 3 months after catheter removal, with an approximately linear dose-response relationship. MUL has good measurement reproducibility and moderate predictive value, supporting its potential as an imaging biomarker for preoperative continence risk stratification in RARP patients.

title: Radiomics is not dead: quantitative imaging in the era of deep learning in renal cell carcinoma.
abstract: A growing consensus in the imaging community holds that radiomics has been rendered obsolete by foundation models and end-to-end deep learning. We disagree, and this perspective explains why. The critics are partially right: inter-operator segmentation variability has compromised reproducibility, methodological quality has been inconsistent, and the gap between published AUCs and clinical implementation has been wide. However, they draw the wrong conclusion. In renal cell carcinoma (RCC), where preoperative contrast-enhanced CT is already standard of care for every patient undergoing nephrectomy and where approximately 30% will recur after surgery, radiomics remain an immediately actionable, interpretable, and deployable non-invasive prognostic tool available. We argue that its primary technical limitation (segmentation variability) is being eliminated by the same deep learning technology used to argue against it: automated segmentation frameworks such as nnU-Net achieve Dice coefficients exceeding 0.93 on external cohorts, removing inter-operator noise. We further argue that in low-prevalence, high-stakes oncological settings, the data volumes required to pre-train foundation models do not exist, and that interpretability - now a regulatory requirement under the EU AI Act for high-risk clinical AI systems - is native to handcrafted radiomics and must be retrofitted onto deep learning architectures. Most critically, we present biological evidence that CT images encode tumor microenvironmental and molecular information invisible to the human eye. This generates a directly testable hypothesis: that preoperative radiomic scores can predict not only recurrence but also likelihood of benefit from adjuvant treatment. Radiomics is not dead. It is, at last, being done properly.

title: Case Report: Multimodal treatment of cervical intramedullary spinal cord metastasis from gastric adenocarcinoma.
abstract: Background Intramedullary spinal cord metastasis (ISCM) from gastric adenocarcinoma is extremely rare, and treatment is not standardized. Case presentation A 59-year-old man with a 22-month history of gastric adenocarcinoma developed acute quadriplegia during systemic therapy. Contrast-enhanced MRI showed a C3-C4 intramedullary enhancing lesion with extensive edema, and ISCM was suspected on clinical and radiological grounds. Because of the high cervical location and surgical risk, the patient received intensity-modulated radiotherapy (40 Gy in 20 fractions) with sintilimab, nab-paclitaxel, and capecitabine; dexamethasone and mannitol were used for spinal cord edema. Grade 4 neutropenia with febrile neutropenia occurred on radiotherapy day 3, and chemotherapy was stopped. Neurological function improved by radiotherapy day 10. Follow-up cervical MRI showed complete radiographic resolution of the lesion, and limb strength recovered to grade 5. The patient died approximately 6 months after the suspected ISCM diagnosis, about 3 weeks after the last cervical MRI; death was clinically attributed to cachexia from systemic tumor progression, without autopsy. Conclusion This case showed temporary neurological and radiographic improvement after a multimodal non-surgical approach, but it does not establish the efficacy of an individual treatment component or an overall survival benefit.

title: Artificial intelligence in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging: a mini review of current applications and future directions.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is creating new opportunities to enhance medical imaging in pediatric oncology through quantitative image analysis and clinical decision support. This mini review examines the emerging role of AI in pediatric head and neck tumor imaging, including applications in lesion detection and characterization, tumor segmentation and volumetric analysis, treatment planning, longitudinal surveillance, prognostication, and precision medicine. Particular attention is given to the challenges of translating these approaches to pediatric populations, where rare and heterogeneous tumors, limited datasets, variable imaging protocols, and insufficient multicenter validation remain important barriers. We also discuss emerging strategies that may facilitate clinical translation, including federated learning, multimodal data integration, explainable AI, and integration with existing radiology workflows. Although pediatric-specific evidence remains limited, continued multicenter collaboration and prospective validation may enable AI-based tools to provide more reproducible quantitative imaging assessment and increasingly personalized clinical decision support. Ultimately, the clinical value of these technologies will depend on their ability to augment radiologist expertise and improve patient care through responsible integration into routine practice.

title: Primary hydatid disease of the rib mimicking a chest wall tumor: a case report and structured review of the literature.
abstract: Rationale Bone hydatid disease is rare, accounting for only 0.5% to 2.5% of all hydatid localizations, and costal (rib) involvement represents only a small fraction of these bone cases. Because clinical and radiological features are nonspecific, rib echinococcosis is easily mistaken for a primary or secondary bone tumor, and the diagnosis is frequently established only after surgical exploration. Case presentation A 60-year-old woman, a farmer from a rural, endemic area of northwestern Tunisia, presented with a painless, slowly enlarging swelling over the eighth right rib of two months' duration, unaccompanied by fever, weight loss, or other systemic symptoms. Ultrasonography and computed tomography of the chest wall showed an expansile osteolytic lesion of the eighth rib with cortical rupture, heterogeneous multiloculated fluid content, and an exophytic vesicle; mild hypereosinophilia was present and hydatid serology (ELISA) was moderately positive. Plasmacytoma/myeloma and bone metastasis were excluded by protein electrophoresis, breast imaging and positron emission tomography. Intraoperative findings and parasitological examination of the cyst fluid (protoscoleces and hooklets) confirmed cystic echinococcosis. A diagnosis of primary costal cystic echinococcosis was retained. Interventions The patient underwent a right lateral thoracotomy centered on the lesion with segmental resection of the affected eighth rib, debridement of adjacent soft tissue, and 20% hypertonic saline protection and irrigation to prevent local seeding, followed by three 1-month cycles of oral albendazole (400 mg twice daily). Outcomes The postoperative course was uneventful. The patient was discharged on postoperative day three and remained symptom-free, with no clinical, imaging or serological evidence of recurrence at two years of structured follow-up (clinical examination, chest-wall ultrasonography, CT and serology, the ELISA becoming negative at 24 months). Conclusion Rib hydatidosis should be included in the differential diagnosis of an osteolytic costal lesion in patients from endemic areas, even when systemic symptoms and inflammatory markers are absent and serology is negative. In our experience, complete segmental resection respecting the principles of hydatid surgery, combined with albendazole, was associated with a favorable outcome at 2 years; longer follow-up is required because late recurrences of bone echinococcosis are well documented.

title: Case Report: Long-term follow-up in ulnar-mammary syndrome caused by novel TBX3 variants: a case series with longitudinal endocrine follow-up.
abstract: Background Ulnar-mammary syndrome (UMS; MIM 181450) is a rare autosomal-dominant disorder with incomplete penetrance affecting multiple body systems, including the upper limbs, apocrine glands, teeth, hair, and genitals. Long-term natural history data are scarce, as most reported cases lack sustained clinical follow-up. This report describes two pediatric patients with UMS harboring novel TBX3 variants, with a focus on the endocrine trajectory in one case. Case description We report two male patients diagnosed with UMS at 12 years of age. Patient 1 (P1) was previously reported in a Chinese-language case description at his initial presentation (Wang et al., 2020); the present report extends that case with longitudinal data through age 16 and adds a second patient. P1 presented with slow growth velocity, delayed puberty, and characteristic dysmorphic features including mammary gland hypoplasia and apocrine glands. Genetic testing identified a de novo frameshift variant in TBX3 (c.711del p.N238Mfs*4). He received recombinant human growth hormone (rhGH) therapy for approximately 2.5 years. On longitudinal follow-up until age 16, GH secretory responses normalized on repeat testing and pituitary hypoplasia was no longer evident on MRI. The initial suspicion of isolated hypogonadotropic hypogonadism (IHH) was revised to constitutional delay of growth and puberty (CDGP) after spontaneous puberty commenced at age 15 and progressed. Patient 2 (P2) presented with pubertal delay and mammary gland hypoplasia without facial dysmorphism, and was found to have a de novo splice-site variant (c.658-3C>G). A minigene assay confirmed that this variant disrupts normal mRNA splicing, generating two aberrant transcripts that are predicted to result in loss of TBX3 function. He had been treated with rhGH at an outside hospital from age 10 years and 10 months for approximately one year; repeat GH stimulation testing at our institution after a > 5-month wash-out period showed a normal peak GH of 14.1 μg/L. rhGH was re-initiated due to documented growth arrest, with progressive dose titration and a partial growth response observed through age 14 years and 8 months (height 161.7 cm). Conclusion This case series expands the mutational spectrum of UMS with two novel TBX3 variants and provides longitudinal observational data suggesting that GH deficiency and pituitary hypoplasia in UMS may not be permanent in all patients, and that some cases of presumed IHH may represent CDGP. These findings emphasize the potential value of long-term monitoring in UMS to better characterize disease evolution and avoid premature conclusions about endocrine prognosis. The main limitations are the retrospective, two-case design.

title: Association of preoperative frailty, inflammatory markers and CT radiomics with complications after esophagectomy in older adults: a five-year retrospective analysis and online dynamic nomogram development.
abstract: Objective Older adults with esophageal cancer have poor physiological tolerance and a high risk of postoperative complications. This study examined whether preoperative frailty, hematologic inflammatory indices and CT radiomic features independently predict these complications and built a validated web-based nomogram for personalized risk prediction. Methods This five-year retrospective study included 526 patients aged at least 60 years who underwent radical esophagectomy between 2019 and 2023. Frailty was assessed with the Fried phenotype, five inflammatory indices were calculated from preoperative blood counts, and CT radiomic features were extracted from contrast-enhanced chest CT. Because the five indices share the same four cell counts, their collinearity was diagnosed and the indices were compared through sequential selection, single-index and alternative-model discrimination, reclassification metrics, and order-reversed and bootstrap validation. Independent predictors were identified by two-stage multivariable logistic regression, ranked with SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP), and assembled into a nomogram; discrimination, calibration and net clinical benefit were evaluated in training and validation cohorts. Results Complications occurred in 187 of 526 patients (35.55%). The five inflammatory indices were strongly collinear; across all sensitivity analyses the systemic inflammation response index and systemic immune-inflammation index were retained independently of entry order, whereas the neutrophil-, platelet- and monocyte-to-lymphocyte ratios added no incremental information. Frailty, the two retained composite indices and three CT radiomic features (lesion texture heterogeneity, gray-level mean value and shape irregularity) were independent predictors, with frailty carrying the greatest SHAP weight. The nomogram achieved areas under the receiver operating characteristic curve of 0.824 (95% confidence interval 0.780-0.868) and 0.807 (0.746-0.868) in the training and validation cohorts, with good calibration and net clinical benefit, and it was implemented as a web tool. Conclusion Preoperative frailty, inflammatory indices and CT radiomic features are independent predictors of postoperative complications, with distinct contributions revealed by SHAP. The validated web nomogram reliably stratifies risk and supports individualized perioperative management.

title: AV-MapNet: geodesic vessel tokenization and sequential refinement for retinal vessel segmentation and artery-vein classification.
abstract: Accurate retinal vessel segmentation and artery-vein (A/V) classification are important for quantitative analysis of retinal vascular morphology, yet remain challenging in thin vessels, bifurcations, crossings, low-contrast regions, and pathological structures. This work proposes AV-MapNet, a structure-aware deep learning framework that integrates multi-scale vessel extraction, sequential residual refinement, Geodesic Vessel Tokenization (GVT), topology-aware token reasoning, and vessel-guided A/V classification. The retinal vascular tree is first extracted using a residual encoder-decoder with multi-scale dilated context and progressively corrected through recurrent vessel refinement. GVT then organizes intermediate features into vessel-aligned tokens according to refined vessel probability, local orientation, boundary ambiguity, and junction information using differentiable geodesic propagation. The resulting tokens undergo structure-biased long-range reasoning and are reconstructed into dense contextual features for subsequent A/V classification. Independent artery and vein branches are conditioned on the refined vessel representation and undergo class-specific sequential refinement before joint normalization. AV-MapNet achieved vessel segmentation DSC values of 83.01%, 85.21%, and 87.10% on RITE, HRF, and DRIVE, respectively, with corresponding accuracies of 97.67%, 98.01%, and 98.52%. Structural evaluation on the 20-image DRIVE test set yielded a clDice of 0.8490±0.0194 , with Betti-0 and Betti-1 errors of 0.9071±0.1890 and 0.2391±0.1066 , respectively. For direct binary A/V classification on valid labelled vessel pixels, AV-MapNet achieved accuracies of 96.01%, 96.48%, and 97.20% on LES-AV, AV-DRIVE, and RITE, respectively. These results demonstrate that combining sequential refinement with vessel-conditioned geodesic representation provides an effective framework for structurally informed retinal vascular analysis.

title: Structural and functional network changes following thalamotomy for focal dystonia: a multimodal MRI study.
abstract: Converging evidence supports dystonia as a disorder of large-scale brain networks arising from dysfunction within, or impaired communication between, nodes of the cortico-basal ganglia-thalamo-cortical and cerebello-thalamo-cortical circuits. Focal hand dystonia is associated with abnormalities across cortical and subcortical networks. High intensity focused ultrasound (HiFU) offers a novel therapeutic approach that provides an opportunity to examine treatment related structural and functional network changes. Eleven individuals with focal hand dystonia, of musician's dystonia and writer's cramp subtype, underwent multimodal MRI, including structural analysis, diffusion tensor imaging (DTI), and resting-state functional MRI (rs-fMRI) at baseline, with comparison made to ten age- and sex-matched healthy control participants. These imaging metrics were repeated at 1, 3 and 12 months following HiFU ventro-oral (Vo)-complex thalamotomy. This trial was registered with the Australia New Zealand Clinical Trials Registry (ACTRN12622000775718p). No differences in regional volumes were observed at baseline between the groups. Following thalamotomy, small uncorrected volumetric changes were noted in several regions of interest, and DTI demonstrated lower tract-wise fractional anisotropy (FA) and coefficient of linearity (CL) within the treated pallidothalamic tract, with node-wise analysis demonstrating focal microstructural alterations that were most apparent at 12 months following treatment. There were no corresponding changes in fronto-striatal or fronto-thalamic tracts. rs-fMRI revealed baseline alterations in intra- and inter-network connectivity involving sensorimotor, visual, attentional, default mode and executive networks. Following thalamotomy, changes in functional connectivity were modest and temporally variable, without evidence of large-scale network reorganisation. These findings suggest that focal hand dystonia is associated with distributed functional network dysfunction, in the context of preserved macroscopic structure. We propose that Vo-complex thalamotomy is associated with focal, localized microstructural alterations within the pallidothalamic tract, most notable at 12 months, which may contribute to modulation of pathological pallidothalamic drive rather than widespread restoration of functional network connectivity.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging-based artificial intelligence in identifying imaging phenotypes of non-secondary trigeminal neuralgia: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Conventional visual magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) assessment of neurovascular compression may overlook subtle trigeminal nerve abnormalities. We evaluated the pooled discriminative performance of MRI-based artificial intelligence (AI) models for identifying pain-related trigeminal nerve phenotypes in non-secondary trigeminal neuralgia. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, and the Cochrane Library were searched from inception to April 2026. Eligible studies developed or validated MRI-based radiomics or AI models and provided sufficient information to construct or approximate 2 × 2 contingency tables. Risk of bias was assessed using the Quality Assessment of Diagnostic Accuracy Studies 2 (QUADAS-2) tool. Sensitivity and specificity were jointly pooled using a bivariate random-effects model, and a summary receiver operating characteristic curve was constructed. Results Eight studies comprising 628 nerve-level observations (298 symptomatic or affected nerves and 330 comparator nerves) were included. Pooled sensitivity was 0.83 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.78-0.87), pooled specificity was 0.81 (95% CI, 0.74-0.86), and the summary area under the curve was 0.86 (95% CI, 0.82-0.88). Results remained stable after leave-one-out analysis. Radiomics-only models and models combining radiomic and anatomical features showed broadly comparable performance. Conclusions Preliminary evidence suggests that MRI-based AI models provide moderate discriminative ability for identifying the affected nerve side in trigeminal neuralgia, with relatively stable sensitivity but lower specificity. Given the limited number of studies, particularly in subgroup analyses, these findings should be interpreted cautiously. Such models may currently serve as adjunctive imaging tools. Larger multicenter studies with independent external validation and clinically relevant reference standards are needed.

title: Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus: from pathophysiological mechanisms to precision diagnosis and optimized therapeutic outcomes.
abstract: Background Idiopathic normal pressure hydrocephalus (iNPH) is a potentially reversible neurological disorder of older adults, characterized by the classic triad of gait disturbance, cognitive impairment, and urinary incontinence. Despite its treatable nature, iNPH remains widely underdiagnosed, and the prediction of shunt responsiveness and optimization of therapeutic outcomes remain major clinical challenges. Methods We conducted a narrative review informed by a structured PubMed search of studies published between January 2017 and June 2026. Forty-eight original clinical studies, including randomized controlled trials (RCTs), prospective and retrospective cohort studies, and cross-sectional studies addressing the pathophysiology, diagnosis, treatment, or prognosis of iNPH, were selected for synthesis; foundational trials and guidelines published before 2017 were cited for context. Results Emerging, largely correlational evidence links iNPH to impaired glymphatic function, perivascular aquaporin-4 loss, and delayed cerebrospinal fluid (CSF) tracer clearance, although causality remains unproven. Instrumented gait analysis, MRI volumetry, and refined CSF tap test protocols may improve the objectivity of patient evaluation, but most of these tools have been validated only in small single-center cohorts. The first large placebo-controlled RCT (PENS) confirmed gait improvement after shunt surgery, extending earlier evidence from the Japanese SINPHONI and SINPHONI-2 studies, whereas acetazolamide showed no benefit in the DRAIN trial. Adjuvant rehabilitation may enhance gait recovery and reduce fall risk. Multiple clinical, imaging, and neuropsychological predictors of shunt responsiveness have been reported, but no single biomarker achieves sufficient predictive accuracy, and heterogeneity in diagnostic criteria, outcome measures, and follow-up limits comparisons across studies. Conclusion Shunt surgery is now supported by randomized evidence for gait outcomes, whereas most diagnostic and prognostic biomarkers remain investigational. Priorities include standardized diagnostic pathways, prospective external validation of multimodal prognostic models, incorporation of patient-reported and caregiver outcomes, and equitable access to specialized care.

Priorities include standardized diagnostic pathways, prospective external validation of multimodal prognostic models, incorporation of patient-reported and caregiver outcomes, and equitable access to specialized care.

title: LARU-net: lesion-aware residual attention U-net for binary cucumber leaf lesion segmentation and continuous severity estimation.
abstract: Plant leaf diseases threaten agricultural productivity and motivate accurate automated monitoring. This study presents LARU-Net, a unified architecture for binary cucumber lesion segmentation (lesion versus background) with an auxiliary continuous severity-regression output on a bounded 0-4 scale. The network integrates a Disease Feature Enhancement Autoencoder, Residual Multi-Scale Encoder, transformer bottleneck, Attention-Guided Decoder, and Boundary Refinement Module. On the declared held-out test partition (1,080 images), the archived full-model results were Dice 0.9230, IoU 0.8660, Boundary F1 0.9350, and precision 0.9460; the previously emphasized Dice value of 0.9456 is a validation value and is now identified as such. Severity estimates yielded an overall MAE of 0.29, RMSE of 0.37, and R 2 of 0.90. These values are single-run point estimates from one greenhouse image collection. Plant/session identifiers, complete acquisition and annotation provenance, repeated-run logs, and an external dataset were not preserved in the supplied study archive; therefore, the results support in-domain evaluation but not broad cross-greenhouse or cross-season generalization. The split was stratified at image level; independence at plant, leaf, or acquisition-session level could not be verified. Confidence intervals and significance tests were not reconstructed because per-image predictions and repeated-run logs were unavailable.

title: StoneXAI-Net: an explainable weakly supervised framework for kidney stone classification, localization, and segmentation from CT images.
abstract: Introduction Kidney stone disease (urolithiasis) is one of the most frequent urological diseases worldwide; it is highly recurrent and carries a significant clinical burden and economic cost. Non-contrast computed tomography (CT) is the primary diagnostic modality and offers the highest sensitivity and specificity. However, automated kidney stone analysis remains challenging because expert pixel-level annotations are scarce, hyperdense non-stone anatomy causes mislocalization in weakly supervised localization, and explainable artificial intelligence (XAI) methods are often used circularly, both for weakly supervised localization and for its subsequent interpretation. Methods We present StoneXAI-Net, an explainable, weakly supervised framework to classify, localize, and segment kidney stones from CT images. The framework consists of three modules: (i) a CT-physics augmentation strategy that diversifies training and mitigates overfitting; (ii) consensus pseudo-labeling that combines complementary explanation maps with uncertainty maps and anatomical priors to suppress false localizations; and (iii) a faithfulness audit module with deletion, insertion, and pointing-game metrics that objectively evaluates explanation quality. The resulting consensus pseudo-labels were used to train an attention-prior-conditioned Attention U-Net for segmentation. The framework was evaluated on 3,364 axial abdominal CT images (1,577 stone and 1,787 normal) using five-fold cross-validation. Results StoneXAI-Net achieved 97.4% accuracy, 98.4% precision, 96.0% recall, a 97.1% F1-score, and a 99.5% AUC. Against consensus pseudo-masks, the full segmentation configuration achieved a proxy Dice coefficient of 0.834, an IoU of 0.777, and an HD95 of 2.94 px; anatomical post-processing reduced HD95 by 6.26 px. Discussion StoneXAI-Net is a feasible and interpretable framework for the automated analysis of kidney stones that substantially reduces the time-consuming and costly manual annotation of kidney stones by experts. Because segmentation was evaluated against pseudo-masks at the slice level, these results are proxy estimates that require confirmation with expert annotations and patient-level validation.

title: Hybrid one-shot and vertical federated learning framework for privacy-preserving brain tumor classification and segmentation using the BRISC2025 dataset.
abstract: Introduction From MRI images, diagnosis of brain tumors may have limitations due to restriction over patient privacy and lack of annotated datasets so that models cannot be trained across multiple institutions. Methods HOS-VFL: A Hybrid One-Shot and Vertical Federated Learning framework with a two-round protocol that jointly enjoys the advantages of prototype-based one-shot aggregation and encrypted vertical feature space augmentation. Tested on BRISC2025 MRimages of glioma, meningioma, pituitary and non-tumor, with T1-weighted images, expert-annotated, at five simulated institutions, with simulated IID and Dirichlet setups. Results HOS-VFL obtained values of 98.73% on accuracy and 35-50 for conventional federated learning, with a 94.3% reduction compared to the best baseline valued. HOS-VFL performed 98.73% accuracy and 35-50 for the conventional federated learning with an improvement of 94.3% when compared with its best baseline accuracy. The mean Dice and IoU of Segmentation was 0.9147, 0.8423 respectively. Performance did not wane differently in terms of competitive levels and number of institutions, and was able to withstand gradient inference attacks. Discussion HOS-VFL philosophy is centralised performance with minimum communication with retention of raw data local. The method needs to be validated on larger real multi-center datasets before their clinical use.

title: Hemodynamic changes after artificial vessel reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm: a case report.
abstract: Objectives Isolated iliac artery aneurysms (IIAA) frequently coexist with abdominal aortic aneurysms (AAA), yet their causal association remains unclear. This study aimed to investigate hemodynamic alterations following artificial vessel reconstruction for iliac aneurysm and its impact on the abdominal aorta and iliac artery. Case presentation A 54-year-old man with a history of thyroid adenoma presented with left lower abdominal pain. Computed tomography angiography (CTA) revealed an aneurysm involving the entire left common iliac artery (48 mm × 55 mm × 81 mm). The patient was hemodynamically stable, with unremarkable physical examination and laboratory findings. He underwent aneurysm resection and aortoiliac reconstruction with a synthetic graft. Intraoperatively, arterial tortuosity and marked dilation at the bifurcation were noted. Postoperative CTA confirmed graft patency, and the patient recovered uneventfully. Preoperative and postoperative CTA scans were used for three-dimensional vascular reconstruction, followed by computational fluid dynamics (CFD) to assess hemodynamic parameters including wall shear stress (WSS), blood pressure, and flow velocity. Conclusion Prosthetic vascular reconstruction for common iliac artery aneurysm (CIAA) may produce dual hemodynamic effects on the abdominal aorta. While the causal link between CIAA and AAA is unproven, the surgery eliminates rupture risk of the target aneurysm. These exploratory results may provide hemodynamic references to optimize surgical planning for iliac artery aneurysms.

title: Endoscope-assisted vs. conventional anterior cervical discectomy and fusion for single-level degenerative cervical disease: a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Background Endoscope-assisted anterior cervical discectomy and fusion (EA-ACDF) has been introduced as a modified technique for the treatment of degenerative cervical disease, but its comparative efficacy and safety relative to conventional ACDF (CA-ACDF) remain uncertain. This systematic review and meta-analysis aimed to compare EA-ACDF with CA-ACDF for single-level degenerative cervical disease. Methods PubMed, Embase, Web of Science, the Cochrane Library, CNKI, WanFang, VIP, and SinoMed were searched from inception through September 7, 2026. Comparative studies of EA-ACDF vs. CA-ACDF were included. Random-effects meta-analyses were performed. Methodological quality was assessed using the Newcastle-Ottawa Scale, and certainty of evidence was evaluated using GRADE. Results Eleven retrospective comparative studies involving 755 patients were included. Compared with CA-ACDF, EA-ACDF was associated with longer operative time (MD = 17.31 min, 95% CI 11.38-23.23), but lower intraoperative blood loss (MD = -17.31 mL, 95% CI -24.38 to -10.25), postoperative drainage volume (MD = -10.97 mL, 95% CI -16.98 to -4.96), length of hospital stay (MD = -0.67 days, 95% CI -1.16 to -0.17), and overall complication rate (RR = 0.44, 95% CI 0.25-0.78). No significant between-group differences were observed in final Japanese Orthopaedic Association score, Neck Disability Index, visual analogue scale score, cervical lordosis, or fusion rate. The certainty of evidence ranged from low to very low. Conclusion EA-ACDF may offer modest perioperative advantages at the cost of longer operative time, while short- to mid-term clinical, radiographic, and fusion outcomes appear broadly similar. Current evidence does not establish clinical superiority. Systematic review registration https://www.crd.york.ac.uk/PROSPERO/view/CRD420251123475, identifier CRD420251123475.

title: Computer-Aided Diagnosis System for Sow Pregnancy Using Low-Frequency Portable Ultrasound Videos with Preprocessing and Augmentation Techniques.
abstract: Accurate pregnancy diagnosis is important for reproductive management in pig farming. This study evaluated a computer-aided diagnosis workflow using portable low-frequency ultrasound videos from 1895 sows at two sites. Xception frame predictions were aggregated into video-level decisions. Original, Preprocessing (wavelet denoising and contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization), Mixup, and their combination (Combined) were compared across ten repeated sow-level splits. Combined achieved mean accuracies of 84.5% and 85.3% in Datasets A and B, respectively, with pregnant-sow videos restricted to days 18-25 post-insemination. Compared with Original, mean specificity increased by 1.3 and 2.4 percentage points and Youden's index by 1.7 and 2.3 points, while mean sensitivity was numerically similar. Paired 95% confidence intervals for specificity and Youden's index differences excluded zero only in Dataset B, without adjustment for multiple comparisons. Paired comparisons of the area under the curve (AUC) did not establish improved discrimination. Mixup yielded the highest mean specificity and AUC, whereas Combined yielded higher mean sensitivity than Mixup. This trade-off varied across partition subsets. Cross-site and leave-one-session-out evaluations showed performance variability across acquisition settings, with no consistently best condition. These comparisons identify configuration-dependent trade-offs requiring further evaluation for diagnostic support.

title: From Silver Stains to Deep Learning: Neurohistological Analysis and Digital Mapping of the Brain of Domestic and Laboratory Animals in Veterinary Neuroscience.
abstract: Neurohistological analysis has evolved from descriptive microscopy and classical staining toward quantitative, standardized, and increasingly automated approaches. This narrative review traces this evolution in domestic animals, such as dogs, cats, horses, cattle, pigs, sheep, and goats, with humans and common laboratory animals as methodological comparators, based on the literature retrieved from PubMed, Scopus, and Web of Science. Gross dissection, selective staining, immunohistochemistry, and neuronal tracing progressively expanded the structural and neurochemical information obtainable from the brain, while macroscopic and microscopic morphometry, including design-based stereology, enabled unbiased estimation of brain volumes and cell numbers. Digital microscopy made histological slides computable, and machine learning and deep learning now allow automated segmentation directly from raw images, while magnetic resonance imaging and spatial transcriptomics link histology to connectivity and gene expression. However, direct evidence in domestic animals remains restricted to a few species and brain regions: annotated collections are scarce, data are poorly integrated, and most tools are calibrated on human, mouse, or rat brains. Open resources such as the CytoDArk0 dataset and the CISCA segmentation method are early steps forward. Progress will require species-specific brain atlases, shared protocols, and validated, interpretable methods that treat anatomical differences between species as biological information rather than noise.

title: From Anatomical Representation to Quantitative Measurement: A Deep Learning-Based Multi-View Framework for Automated Cardiac Size Assessment in Canine Thoracic Radiographs.
abstract: Accurate and reproducible quantitative assessment of cardiac size from thoracic radiographs remains challenging because conventional measurements require manual identification of multiple anatomical structures and geometric relationships. This study develops an automated multi-view image analysis system for quantitative cardiac measurement in canine thoracic radiographs. The proposed system integrates anatomical segmentation, keypoint localization, geometric measurement, and quantitative agreement analysis into a unified computational workflow. For lateral radiographs, an RSMF-DeepLabV3+ network was developed to segment the cardiac silhouette and thoracic vertebral structures for automated Vertebral Heart Size (VHS) calculation. A cross-sectional search strategy was introduced to constrain cardiac short-axis determination according to the geometric requirements of VHS measurement. For ventrodorsal/dorsoventral radiographs, YOLOv11-Pose was employed to localize predefined anatomical landmarks for automated cardiothoracic ratio (CTR) estimation. On the independent test sets, the automated VHS measurement achieved a Pearson correlation coefficient of 0.8767 and an ICC of 0.8744 with manual reference measurements, while the corresponding values for CTR were 0.8557 and 0.7928, respectively. Bland-Altman analysis was additionally used to characterize the agreement and measurement differences between automated and manual results. These findings demonstrate the feasibility of integrating deep learning-based anatomical analysis and geometry-based measurement for automated cardiac size quantification from complementary radiographic views. The proposed framework provides a computer-aided approach for standardized multi-view quantitative assessment of cardiac size in veterinary thoracic radiography.

title: What Radiomics Teaches Us About Vestibular Schwannoma Biology: Imaging Biomarkers, Artificial Intelligence, and Future Clinical Translation: A Narrative Review.
abstract: Background/Objective: Vestibular schwannoma is a benign Schwann cell tumor characterized by marked biological and clinical heterogeneity, resulting in highly variable growth patterns, hearing outcomes and treatment responses. Advances in molecular biology have improved the understanding of the pathways driving tumor development, highlighting the roles of NF2-related signaling, angiogenesis, inflammation and tumor-microenvironment interactions. In parallel, quantitative imaging, radiomics, and artificial intelligence (AI) are being investigated for tumor characterization and outcome prediction, although the biological specificity of many imaging-derived features remains unproven. Methods: This narrative review was conducted by examining recent literature on the role of radiomics in Vestibular schwannoma biology. Results: Across published studies reviewed we summarize the current knowledge on vestibular schwannoma biology and discusses the clinical potential of quantitative MRI, volumetric analysis, radiomics and AI for tumor characterization, growth prediction, treatment-response assessment, automated segmentation and functional outcome prediction. Conclusions: Particular emphasis is placed on distinguishing reported predictive associations from validated biological correlates and on the potential value of integrating imaging with molecular data. Finally, current limitations, including methodological heterogeneity, lack of standardization and the need for multicenter validation, are discussed to outline future directions for clinical translation.

title: Artificial Intelligence for Priority Cancer Control Interventions in Kenya: A Strategic Development Roadmap from Screening to Treatment.
abstract: Cancer now ranks among the leading causes of death in Kenya, with approximately 35,867 new cases and 22,888 deaths annually, and outcomes remain constrained less by the availability of therapy than by the diagnostic pathway that must precede it. A national pathology workforce numbering in the low hundreds serves a population exceeding fifty million, and delayed or absent tissue diagnosis drives late presentation across the five malignancies that account for most of the national burden. Artificial intelligence offers a mechanism to extend interpretive capacity in a system where human expertise cannot be scaled at the rate the disease burden demands. This communication sets out a prioritized research agenda spanning smartphone-assisted visual inspection of the cervix, breast ultrasound classification and histopathological grading, morphological and immunophenotypic triage of hematolymphoid neoplasms, radiomic triage of thoracic and hepatic disease, and AI-assisted radiotherapy contouring. We present a six-stage methodological pipeline covering stakeholder engagement, local dataset curation, transfer learning, validation, usability assessment, and data governance, together with a tiered adoption framework matched to laboratory capability and the workforce competencies required for safe clinical supervision of these systems. The agenda is directed at early-career investigators and is transferable to comparable low- and middle-income settings.

title: Explainable AI-Based Medical Image Segmentation and Radiomics for Brain Disorder Classification over Structural MRI.
abstract: Neuropsychiatric disorders including attention-deficit/hyperactivity disorder (ADHD), bipolar disorder (BD), and schizophrenia (SZ) exhibit significant clinical heterogeneity and overlapping symptom profiles, which severely limits the diagnostic specificity of conventional symptom-based assessments. While structural magnetic resonance imaging (sMRI) provides objective insights into anatomical brain alterations, existing computational frameworks often rely on single-plane or binary patient-control analyses, lack anatomical interpretability, or risk data leakage through inconsistent validation protocols. To address these challenges, this study proposes a segmentation-guided AI framework for medical image processing and recognition that fuses FastSurfer-derived regional handcrafted features encompassing Fourier shape descriptors, two-dimensional wavelet and second-order local directional gradient pattern (LDGP) textures, and ROI-filtered XFeat keypoints with complementary multi-view (axial, sagittal, coronal) EfficientNetB0 deep representations extracted from whole-brain T1-weighted sMRI. The segmentation stage provides anatomically defined regions for radiomic feature extraction, while explainable representations maintain anatomical traceability. A key contribution of this work is its dual evaluation strategy within a unified structural feature space: it addresses both broad transdiagnostic four-class classification (Healthy Control (HC) vs. ADHD vs. BD vs. SZ) and focused binary patient-control contrasts (SZ vs. HC and BD vs. HC). To ensure rigorous evaluation, feature fusion, feature standardisation, Salp Swarm Optimizer (SSO) feature selection, hyperparameter selection, and early stopping are performed exclusively within the training partitions of a participant-level nested cross-validation (five outer and three inner folds), and held-out participants are used only once for evaluation. Evaluated on the UCLA Consortium for Neuropsychiatric Phenomics (CNP) dataset, the framework achieved 79.3% accuracy in four-class transdiagnostic classification. In focused binary tasks, the framework reached 84.3% accuracy for SZ versus HC and 82.7% accuracy for BD versus HC. These results indicate that combining segmentation-guided radiomic descriptors with multi-view deep representations provides a promising research framework for structural MRI analysis of neuropsychiatric disorders, while external validation is required before clinical application.

title: Choriocapillaris Thinning in Myopic Macular Degeneration Revealed by Swept-Source Optical Coherence Tomography C-Scan Imaging.
abstract: Background: The choriocapillaris (CC), which supplies the outer retina, may be involved in myopic macular degeneration (MMD); however, quantitative in vivo assessment remains challenging. This study aimed to quantify CC thickness (CCT) with swept-source optical coherence tomography (SS-OCT) C-scan imaging and to characterize its changes in MMD. Methods: This study grouped participants into control (CN), simple high myopia (SHM), and pathological myopia (PM) groups. Each group included 30 eyes. Swept-source optical coherence tomography was used to obtain 3 × 3 mm volumetric scans. The choriocapillaris was segmented from the en-face (C-scan) images to determine its thickness and its coefficient of variation. The choroidal thickness (CT), luminal volume, stromal volume, and choroidal vascularity index were quantified from the volumetric data. Results: Reproducibility was excellent (intra- and inter-grader ICCs 0.987 and 0.970). CCT was lower in PM than in CN and SHM (mean differences 9.94 µm and 7.95 µm; both p < 0.001) and slightly lower in SHM than in CN (1.99 µm; p = 0.005), together with increased coefficient of variation in PM. CT and axial length were independently associated with CCT (p = 0.002 and 0.020, respectively). Mediation analysis indicated that choroidal thickness accounted for approximately 52.5% of the association between axial length and choriocapillaris thickness (p < 0.05). CCT distinguished PM from SHM with excellent performance (AUC = 0.996; cutoff 8.9 µm). Conclusions: Choriocapillaris thickness was significantly reduced, with increased relative spatially heterogeneous in MMD. It was associated with axial length and choroidal thickness and showed excellent discriminatory performance.

title: Explainable Deep Learning-Based Computer-Aided Differential Diagnosis of Multiple Sclerosis and Neuromyelitis Optica Using 3D MRI Lesion Features.
abstract: Neurological disorders are among the leading causes of disability and mortality worldwide, making timely and accurate diagnosis essential. Differential diagnosis (DD) of Multiple Sclerosis (MS) and Neuromyelitis Optica (NMO) spectrum disorder using brain MRI remains challenging due to overlapping clinical manifestations and similar lesion characteristics. To address this challenge, this study proposes a neuroinformatics-driven computer-aided differential diagnosis (CADD) framework that automatically extracts, encodes, and analyzes quantitative 3D lesion biomarkers from brain MRI using deep learning and interpretable neuroimaging analytics. The proposed framework integrates three artificial intelligence (AI) modules: the NeuroImaging Sequence Examiner (NISE) for MRI sequence identification, the NeuroImaging Volumetric Extractor (NIVE) for skull stripping, and the NeuroImaging Lesion Extractor (NILE) for lesion segmentation. These modules are combined into an end-to-end neuroinformatics framework termed NeuroImaging Differential Evaluation (NIDE), which performs automated neuroimaging processing, lesion biomarker extraction, structured feature encoding, and differential diagnosis. Following lesion segmentation, quantitative 3D morphological and geometric lesion properties are extracted and transformed into a structured neuroimaging representation, where each row corresponds to an individual lesion and each column encodes a specific lesion biomarker. The resulting feature matrix is subsequently classified using a 2D convolutional neural network (2D-CNN). Comparative experiments against 3D-CNN models trained on raw MRI volumes, skull-stripped MRI volumes, lesion-mask volumes, and conventional machine learning classifiers demonstrate the superiority of the proposed lesion-driven learning strategy. Using ResNet50, the proposed framework achieved an accuracy of 80% for MS-NMO spectrum disorder differential diagnosis. Furthermore, the framework is independent of MRI view-plane orientation, enabling robust performance across different imaging orientations while operating in a fully automated manner. Beyond classification performance, the framework provides a structured representation of quantitative lesion biomarkers and enables interpretable neuroimaging analytics through Explainable Artificial Intelligence (XAI), with model interpretations corroborated by expert radiological assessment. The proposed NIDE framework demonstrates how automated neuroimaging processing, quantitative lesion characterization, structured feature encoding, and explainable AI can be integrated into a unified neuroinformatics workflow for differential diagnosis. These findings highlight the potential of neuroinformatics-driven decision-support systems for advancing neuroimaging analysis and clinical management of demyelinating neurological disorders.

title: Assessment of Reflection-Mode Imaging Performance for Ultrasound Computed Tomography Using Tissue-Mimicking Phantoms.
abstract: Ultrasound computed tomography (USCT) has emerged as a promising multi-modal imaging technique, yet standardized phantoms for validating its reflection-mode performance remain lacking, hindering system calibration and cross-platform comparison. In this study, we designed and fabricated a suite of agar-based tissue-mimicking phantoms dedicated to quantitative quality assessment of ring-array USCT reflection imaging. The phantom set consists of three individual modules for evaluating spatial resolution, slice thickness and three-dimensional volumetric accuracy. The acoustic properties of the tissue-mimicking material were characterized for speed of sound and attenuation and complied with standard ultrasound specifications. All experiments were implemented on an NMPA-approved 2048-element ring-array USCT system using synthetic transmit aperture imaging. Experimental results revealed obvious resolution anisotropy of the ring array, with lateral resolution outperforming axial resolution. The measured slice thickness decreased gradually as the radial position from the ring center decreased, and volumetric measurement errors of embedded ovoid targets were controlled within 3.65%. This phantom suite provides quantitative assessment of the principal reflection-mode imaging metrics on one ring-array USCT system; repeatability under phantom repositioning was not evaluated. These results demonstrate the feasibility of the proposed phantoms on a single ring-array system; validation across other USCT architectures remains to be performed.

title: In Vitro Hemodynamic Assessment of a Novel Pulmonary Visceral Pleura (PVP) Transcatheter Aortic Valve Replacement Prototype Based on Optical and Acoustic Measurements.
abstract: Structural valve degradation remains a key limitation of bioprosthetic transcatheter aortic valve replacement (TAVR) devices, whose bovine or porcine pericardium leaflets are prone to calcification and long-term failure. Pulmonary visceral pleura (PVP), a thin, elastin-rich tissue, has emerged as a promising alternative leaflet material. This study presents an in vitro hemodynamic evaluation of a prototype PVP valve under physiologically representative pulsatile flow in a custom benchtop flow loop. A multimodal framework combined four techniques: high-speed imaging with U-Net deep learning segmentation of the geometric orifice area, quantitative Doppler velocity extraction developed on a Verasonics research ultrasound platform, double-pulse particle image velocimetry (PIV) of the downstream flow field, and transvalvular pressure measurement. The PVP valve was compared with a stiff silicone valve representing a stenotic reference condition. At 75 bpm and 5 L/min, the PVP valve reached a peak geometric orifice area of 2.91 cm2, a mean pressure gradient of 4.3 mmHg, and a peak jet velocity of 2.46 m/s, meeting the ASE velocity and gradient criteria for normal prosthetic valve function. The silicone valve opened to 1.1 cm2 with a gradient of 36.9 mmHg, consistent with moderate-to-severe stenosis. The framework provides a basis for characterizing new bioprosthetic valve materials and benchmark data for fluid-structure interaction modeling.

title: LGCF-Net: Local-Global Context Modeling and Decoder-Guided Residual Correction for Retinal Vessel Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate retinal vessel segmentation is important for quantitative assessment of vascular abnormalities in retinopathy of prematurity (ROP), but remains challenging because vessels vary greatly in caliber and spatial extent, while thin branches and continuous trajectories are easily disrupted by complex retinal backgrounds. We propose LGCF-Net, a U-shaped retinal vessel segmentation network with a ResNet34 encoder. A Local-Global Vessel Context (LGVC) module combines local spatial representation with global frequency-domain context through adaptive fusion, while a Decoder-Guided Residual Correction Fusion (DRCF) module uses decoder semantics to extract and selectively compensate complementary encoder details. Cross-entropy, Dice, and clDice losses are jointly employed for pixel-level, region-level, and topology-aware supervision. On the HVDROPDB-BV Neo subset, LGCF-Net achieved the highest F1 scores, improving F1 by 1.59 percentage points over the second-best method. On DRIVE, CHASE_DB1, and HRF, it also obtained the highest F1 scores among all compared methods. These results indicate that LGCF-Net provides an effective approach for retinal vessel segmentation, particularly for premature-infant retinal images.
