title: Do Saliency Maps Look Where a Human Annotator Looks? An Exploratory Gaze-Based Benchmark of Explainable AI for Colonoscopic Polyp Segmentation.
abstract: Explainable AI (XAI) maps are often judged by whether they highlight what a human would look at, but this is rarely tested against recorded eye movements. This exploratory benchmark compared the fixations of a single annotator from the open GazeMedSeg dataset (26,832 fixations on 1000 Kvasir-SEG colonoscopy images, recorded while the annotator located and then scanned a polyp present in every image) with seven attribution methods for three polyp segmentation U-Nets (test Dice 0.829 ± 0.004). The first fixation fell on the polyp in 45% of images and the second in 93% of images, and 85-91% of fixations in each later fixation-order group fell inside it. Over the whole image, decoder-layer Grad-CAM agreed best with gaze among the explanations (correlation 0.62; 0.65 at matched resolution), yet the model's own probability map agreed slightly better (paired difference -0.023, 95% CI -0.032 to -0.013). Inside the lesion, no method showed statistically significant positive residual agreement with gaze after the tested geometry controls. The most faithful methods in deletion-insertion tests (GradientSHAP, Integrated Gradients) were among the least aligned with gaze, but the faithfulness ranking depended on the test protocol, and gradient-based maps failed a model-randomisation check. Gaze-based evaluation of segmentation explanations therefore needs a model-output baseline, resolution-matched maps and geometry-controlled within-lesion analysis; the findings are specific to one annotator, task-directed viewing and one architecture.

title: Deep Learning-Based Classification of Root Fusion Morphology in Maxillary Second Molars on Cone-Beam Computed Tomography: Impact of Image Preprocessing.
abstract: Maxillary second molars with root fusion exhibit considerable anatomical variability that complicates dental treatment planning. Cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) has become an essential imaging modality for evaluating such complex morphology. This study aimed to develop a deep learning (DL)-based computer-aided diagnosis (CAD) system for the automated classification of root fusion types in maxillary second molars, and to systematically evaluate the impact of image preprocessing strategies on model performance. CBCT images from 172 maxillary second molars (3188 two-dimensional slices) were collected and classified into seven root fusion types. A ResNet50 convolutional neural network was trained with tooth-level 5-fold cross-validation. The effects of grayscale bit depth (4096 vs. 256 levels), preprocessing mode (original, binarized, and segmented images), and contrast enhancement techniques (histogram equalization [HE] and contrast-limited adaptive histogram equalization [CLAHE] with varying parameters) on classification accuracy were systematically compared. The model trained on segmented, non-binarized images with 4096 grayscale levels achieved the highest overall accuracy of 91.6%. In descending order of performance: CLAHE-1 (90.5%), CLAHE-3 (90.5%), CLAHE-40 (88.2%), and HE (83.9%). The unprocessed original image group yielded the lowest accuracy (57.5%). A ResNet50-based DL system can effectively classify complex root fusion morphology in maxillary second molars. Preserving the natural radiopacity gradient of CBCT images, rather than applying artificial contrast enhancement, was critical for optimal model performance. These findings provide a reference for preprocessing strategy selection in dental CBCT-based AI systems.

title: Intraoperative Radiographic Visualization of the Schneiderian Membrane Using the Novel Hydraulic Contrast Lift Protocol: A Retrospective Clinical Case Series.
abstract: Background: Limited intraoperative visibility during transcrestal sinus floor elevation complicates assessment of membrane elevation and possible perforation before graft placement. This retrospective case series evaluated the clinical feasibility and preliminary clinical and radiographic outcomes of the Hydraulic Contrast Lift (HCL) protocol. Materials and methods: A retrospective case series was conducted on seven patients treated with the HCL protocol. The technique uses a hydraulic delivery system to inject a radiopaque contrast medium beneath the Schneiderian membrane. Primary procedural endpoints were membrane visualization and controlled elevation without radiographic signs of perforation. Clinical endpoints included integration of the bone substitute, implant osseointegration, and implant survival. Bone height changes were assessed using preoperative cone-beam computed tomography (CBCT) and post-healing periapical radiographs or CBCT. Results: Successful intraoperative membrane visualization was achieved in all seven cases (100%), with no radiographic evidence of Schneiderian membrane perforation. The mean preoperative residual bone height was 4.5 ± 2.0 mm (range: 1.5-8 mm), and the mean postoperative bone height gain was 9.0 ± 3.3 mm (range: 4-12 mm). Five patients (71.4%) received simultaneous implant placement and two (28.6%) underwent delayed placement. All grafted areas showed radiographic continuity with adjacent bone, and all implants achieved successful osseointegration. Implant survival after implant loading (9-47 months; mean: 28.1 ± 12.8 months) was 100%. Conclusions: Within the limitations of this small retrospective case series, the HCL protocol appeared feasible, enabling intraoperative radiographic visualization of the sinus membrane and controlled elevation. No radiographic signs of membrane perforation or clinical complications were observed. Radiographic bone height gain and favorable implant outcomes were documented during follow-up. Larger prospective studies are needed to evaluate safety, reproducibility, and long-term clinical outcomes.

title: SSGNet++: Stage-Aware Generative Augmentation and Ensemble-Guided Pseudo-Labelling for Medical Imaging.
abstract: Limited annotation and class imbalance remain important challenges in medical image analysis. SSGNet++ examines class-specific StyleGAN3 augmentation for classification and an iterative pseudo-labelling pipeline for segmentation, combining predictions from heterogeneous multi-base and multi-head models with optional mask refinement. We evaluate four classification tasks and four segmentation tasks drawn from six public datasets. In the classification experiments, the best tested synthetic-data settings increased accuracy by 3-7 percentage points over real-only training in several dataset settings, although the preferred augmentation ratio varied and larger ratios could reduce performance. The initial segmentation analyses examined single models, ensembles, iterative pseudo-label training, and refinement stages, but reused validation partitions for both model selection and performance reporting; these results are, therefore, exploratory and may be optimistic. Four-seed follow-ups comprised a post-hoc internal split (112 runs) and a partial external-cohort evaluation (64 runs); multi-head gains were uncertain and refinement effects varied by dataset. These follow-ups remain limited by the post-hoc internal split and incomplete external comparisons.

title: DCLCA-UNet: Dynamic Cross-Level Contextual Attention for 3D Medical Image Segmentation.
abstract: Accurate 3D medical image segmentation requires effective integration of encoder details and decoder semantics. However, their relative contributions vary across decoding stages and spatial locations, and attention based only on the current feature pair may provide limited guidance in ambiguous regions. To address these challenges, we propose Dynamic Cross-Level Contextual Attention U-Net (DCLCA-UNet), which reconstructs cross-level context at each decoding stage from the incoming decoder feature and encoder features at the corresponding and shallower levels. The Cross-Level Contextual Attention Fusion (CLCAF) module uses this context to adaptively weight encoder and decoder features before fusion. The Context-Guided Feature Modulation (CGFM) module then reuses the context to refine the fused representation through scaling and additive correction. Experiments on Synapse, BTCV, and BraTS2023 yield average Dice scores of 88.70%, 84.13%, and 92.34%, respectively, with the lowest corresponding average Hausdorff distance (HD) or 95th-percentile Hausdorff distance (HD95) among the compared methods. These improvements are accompanied by increased computational cost. Repeated experiments and evaluation on AMOS22 provide additional evidence of stability and cross-dataset generalization. Ablation studies further assess the contributions of contextual fusion, modulation, and stage-specific context reconstruction. Together, these results support the effectiveness of contextual guidance in volumetric segmentation.

title: Annotation-Free Vision-Language Concept Bottleneck Models for Interpretable Medical Image Classification: A Review.
abstract: Concept Bottleneck Models (CBMs) route predictions through a layer of human-understandable concepts, but classical CBMs need a concept label for every training image, a cost that is high in medicine. Vision-language models (VLMs) remove that requirement because, in a shared image-text embedding space, a large language model can propose candidate concepts and contrastive similarity can score them, with no concept labels. This review surveys annotation-free VLM-based CBMs and their move into clinical imaging. We cover vision-language foundations (CLIP, ALIGN, LLaVA) and trace concept models from early supervised methods (CBM, CEM, TCAV) to versions that work without manual labels (LaBo, Label-Free CBM, PCBM, OpenCBM, VLG-CBM). We then map these foundations to specific medical fields such as radiology, pathology, cardiology, dermatology, and ophthalmology, highlighting the medical VLM-CBMs closest to actual deployment (CBVLM, AdaCBM, ConcepPath, CBM-RAG). We focus on information leakage, in which task information reaches the prediction through the concept layer without being carried by the named concepts. Two of the seven surveyed medical VLM-CBMs test whether their predictions depend on individual concepts, but none measures leakage, and no shared protocol exists. We identify this gap as a central challenge for interpretable medical AI.

title: AI-Assisted Sequential Graf Assessment of Infant Hip Ultrasound: A Retrospective Single-Centre Evaluation in a Referral Cohort.
abstract: Graf-method ultrasound supports early assessment of developmental dysplasia of the hip (DDH). This study assessed a sequential artificial-intelligence-assisted workflow and clinicians' Checklist I decisions with and without computer-aided diagnosis (CAD). This retrospective single-centre study of referred infants used 1803 development images from 679 examinations and separate cohorts of 1024 workflow and 100 reader images; Graf IV hips were excluded. ResTransUNet segmented eight Checklist I structures to assess reportability. Fifteen clinicians assessed the reader images unaided and four weeks later with CAD. Stand-alone Checklist I accuracy was 93.0% (93/100; 95% CI 86.3-96.6). Of 1024 workflow images, 846 received final outputs; Checklist II non-compliance precision was 48.1%. Among accepted images, the non-type-I endpoint had 81.0% accuracy, 82.7% sensitivity and 80.4% specificity; exact Graf-type agreement was 40.1%. Across entering non-type-I images, 167/266 (62.8%) received a correct positive output. Mean absolute errors were 3.59° for the α angle and 11.91° for the β angle, with a β-angle bias of +11.07°. Clinician accuracy was 72.3% unaided and 90.2% assisted-an observed 17.9 percentage-point difference (95% CI 10.0-26.1); 26 correct decisions became incorrect on AI-error cases. The workflow supported Checklist I assessment, but fixed order precludes causal CAD inference; gate failures and angle errors require refinement and prospective evaluation before clinical implementation.

title: Efficient Parallel Implementation of a 3-D MRF-Based Deformable Image Registration Algorithm in Medical Dynamic CT Imaging.
abstract: Registration techniques play a critical role in computer vision and medical image analysis, enabling the alignment of images acquired at different times or from different modalities. The increasing demand for high-resolution and real-time processing necessitates faster deformable registration algorithms; however, many accurate methods remain computationally expensive, limiting their clinical applicability. This work presents three acceleration strategies for a 3D MRF-based deformable image registration algorithm applied to dynamic CT imaging. First, the parallelizable components of the algorithm were identified and parallelized on the CPU using OpenMP. Second, a fully GPU-based implementation using CUDA was developed. Third, a heterogeneous hybrid CPU/GPU implementation was designed to optimally distribute computational tasks across both platforms. Experimental results on the Learn2Reg dataset with images of size (192 × 160 × 256), demonstrate that the hybrid approach achieves the best overall performance by strategically offloading sequential graph-based bottlenecks to the CPU. It achieves a speedup factor of ~9× compared to the Serial implementation while maintaining comparable accuracy, overcoming the severe hardware utilization limits of the fully GPU-based approach and highlighting the challenges of mapping MRF optimization to massively parallel architectures. These results indicate that hybrid computing architectures provide an effective trade-off between computational efficiency and registration accuracy. A graphical user interface was also developed to visualize the registration process and results.

title: Improving Accuracy and Evaluating the Generalizability of Medical Image Classification Using Pseudo-Invisible-Light Images Generated from RGB Images.
abstract: We extend our previous study on extended 5-channel images, which add two pseudo-invisible-light channels, estimated by spectral reconstruction (MST++) and polynomial extrapolation, to the RGB channels. We first ask whether the accuracy gain reflects prior knowledge contributed by the externally trained spectral-reconstruction model or effects that any 5-channel input derived from RGB would produce. For skin cancer classification with a CNN trained from scratch, the proposed input is compared with grayscale-based extensions, duplicated RGB channels, learned pointwise transforms of RGB, and learned projections of the reconstructed spectrum. Duplicating RGB channels alone raised accuracy from 86.49% to 88.27%; learned transforms of RGB did not significantly exceed this level, whereas the proposed input (89.94%) exceeded both; learned projections of the reconstructed spectrum did not differ significantly from it. We then re-evaluate the method on diabetic retinopathy, gastrointestinal, and glaucoma classification with ImageNet-pretrained ResNet50, with wavelengths selected on validation data. The proposed input exceeded RGB by 1.5-2.1 percentage points in all three tasks, as did most wavelength combinations, but these gains were not significant and not distinguishable from the RGB-duplication control; an effect specific to the proposed input remains unestablished there. Computational cost is also reported.

title: Refining Retinal Vessel Segmentation with Conditional Diffusion Models: A Controlled Evaluation on LU-Net+RA Probability Maps.
abstract: Retinal vessel segmentation remains difficult along thin, low-contrast branches. We evaluate a conditional diffusion refiner for probability maps from a lightweight U-Net with reverse attention (LU-Net+RA). A frozen mask autoencoder produces a spatially downsampled multi-channel grid; a global RGB embedding conditions denoising diffusion implicit model (DDIM) updates, followed by frozen decoding. The refiner adds 527,233 parameters to the 1,946,961-parameter backbone. Matched evaluation on CHASE-DB1, DRIVE and HRF uses five training seeds and five sampling seeds. Refined mean Dice was 0.746, 0.790 and 0.666, against coarse values of 0.811, 0.792 and 0.732. Exploratory paired intervals exclude zero in the negative direction. Conditioning variants changed Dice by less than 0.0002. Deterministic encoded-grid refinement and autoencoder fine-tuning narrowed the gap but exceeded the baseline only on DRIVE; spatial residual refinement changed Dice by -0.0001, +0.0058 and +0.0074. Matched out-of-fold training did not establish absence of input shift. Increasing DDIM updates from 50 to 100 doubled refinement time with negligible observed Dice change. An earlier single-run result was not reproduced. Under this controlled protocol, diffusion refinement did not improve LU-Net+RA.

title: Binding Text to Pixels: A Narrative Review of Supervision Granularity in Language-Guided Chest Radiograph Segmentation and Grounding.
abstract: Chest radiographs come with abundant free-text reports but scarce lesion-level annotation, so report text increasingly supervises localization. This structured narrative review, written for model developers, benchmark curators, and evaluators of clinical AI, covers phrase grounding, weakly supervised localization, language-guided segmentation, grounded report generation, and multimodal large language models to September 2026. We propose a five-level granularity ladder, organizing the field by where text binds to the image, not by architecture, as an explanatory framework and testable hypothesis, and show that separating train-time binding from inference-time output exposes the most informative systems. A resource audit classifying each corpus's spatial signal as reader-drawn, image-derived, or report-derived reveals a structural gap: at MIMIC-CXR scale, lesion masks exist only when generated from the reports that supervise the models, and independent reader-drawn masks for multiple lesion types cover 234-902 images, roughly 400 to 1600 times fewer. On the shared MS-CXR benchmark, three studies report one model at 21.5 to 26.6 mean intersection over union, a spread exceeding most between-method differences. Grounded outputs are intended to make AI assertions checkable at the point of care, though prospective evidence is lacking. We specify an anatomy-referenced evaluation, propose federated subgroup evaluation, and recommend reserving reader-drawn masks for evaluation.

title: Survival Prediction from Public Brain Metastasis MRI Cohorts: A Positive-Control and Permutation-Based Feasibility Evaluation.
abstract: Public brain metastasis MRI cohorts are widely used for prognostic modeling, but whether an endpoint is identifiable at the available sample size is rarely tested. We evaluated eight clinical endpoints in two public cohorts, Yale/BraTS-MET (199 patients, 74 deaths) and OpenBTAI/MOLAB (75 patients, all deceased), using lesion-centered nnU-Net encoder embeddings and PyRadiomics features with patient-grouped cross-validation and label permutation. Patient-level infratentorial involvement served as a positive control (balanced accuracy 0.60); the Graded Prognostic Assessment (GPA) score was recoverable from OpenBTAI radiomics (ρ = 0.42), whereas brain age was not recovered in either cohort. Primary tumor type was the only endpoint significant after multiplicity correction (1.3× chance). Survival endpoints were null for clinical models and the planned graph model (C = 0.50, p = 0.49); an exploratory linear model on embeddings reached C ≈ 0.58 ( p = 0.07, uncorrected), which PyRadiomics features did not reproduce. No progression definition remained significant after family-wise correction. In simulation, 80% power required a true C-index of about 0.68-0.76, so null survival results cannot exclude moderate effects. GPA did not stratify survival ( p = 0.18) in a cohort containing only deceased patients. An extraction error found during revision was corrected.

title: Metric Positional Encoding in Transformer-Based 3D Medical Image Segmentation Under Controlled Spacing Changes.
abstract: In 3D computed tomography segmentation, differences in voxel spacing mean that equal separations on the voxel grid correspond to different physical distances. Many Transformers incorporate positional encodings because self-attention does not explicitly represent position. However, index-based encodings do not express these distances. Whether metric coordinates improve performance or the response to resampling remains unclear. We evaluated this effect using a factorial UNETR design that combined index or physical coordinates with additive Fourier encoding or 3D RoPE. In KiTS23, we evaluated 391 patients across three folds; 117 were resampled to inter-slice spacings of 3, 4, and 5 mm. Control conditions varied the supplied spacing without altering the image. We repeated the RoPE comparison after training the models from scratch on AMOS22-CT. Among the 117 eligible KiTS23 cases, the metric variants responded to the supplied spacing, but no average advantage in Surface Dice change after resampling was demonstrated (contrast: -0.0029; 95% CI: -0.0104 to 0.0043). In 38 eligible AMOS22-CT cases, metric RoPE maintained higher absolute Surface Dice than index-based RoPE, although its advantage decreased from 0.0512 at the original spacing to 0.0216 at 5 mm. The change in Surface Dice from the original-spacing condition was less favorable for metric RoPE (contrast: -0.0241; 95% CI: -0.0296 to -0.0186). For the evaluated models, metric coordinates did not demonstrate a more favorable response to retrospective resampling, despite sensitivity to supplied spacing and higher absolute Surface Dice in AMOS22-CT. The 95% confidence intervals quantify uncertainty due to patient sampling conditional on the trained models; they do not capture variability across training runs.

title: ImageBR: A Public MRI Dataset for Planned Implant Region and Mammary Gland Segmentation in Breast Reconstruction.
abstract: Breast magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) offers three-dimensional anatomical information for reconstruction-oriented analysis, but annotated public datasets targeting implant-based reconstruction are limited. ImageBR contains MRI volumes from 44 patients (26 bilateral and 18 unilateral reconstruction cases), yielding 70 breast-level samples with expert annotations of planned implant regions, mammary gland tissue, and breast regions. The planned implant region is a surgeon-defined virtual surgical target rather than a directly visible anatomical structure on MRI, and its reference annotations were established without using the final prosthesis specifications. A two-stage benchmark combines breast-region extraction with an nnU-Net 3D cascade incorporating image-derived anatomical priors and weighted loss optimization. Under patient-level three-fold cross-validation, the reported mean breast-level Dice scores were 83.0% and 74.4% for planned implant region and mammary gland segmentation, respectively. The retrospective comparison of predicted-region volume and diameter with final implanted prosthesis specifications yielded relative errors of 14.27% and 8.98%, respectively, and measures consistency rather than independent implant-selection accuracy.

title: Probability-Level Fusion of Meta-Information and Multimodal MRI/PET Radiomics for Predicting 1p/19q Codeletion and IDH Mutation in Gliomas.
abstract: Noninvasive prediction of 1p/19q codeletion and isocitrate dehydrogenase (IDH) mutation may support preoperative assessment of lower-grade gliomas. We evaluated leakage-aware probability-level fusion of meta-information and multimodal radiomics. This retrospective study included 217 patients with World Health Organization grade II or III gliomas and preoperative magnetic resonance imaging and positron emission tomography. Meta-information and radiomics models were developed separately, and their calibrated probabilities were combined using weighted averaging or logit stacking. Performance was evaluated using repeated stratified five-fold nested cross-validation with 10 seeds, with all data-dependent procedures confined to training data. For 1p/19q codeletion, weighted averaging achieved an outer-fold area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.816 ± 0.056 (mean ± standard deviation), and both fusion approaches achieved higher patient-level AUCs than meta-information alone after Holm correction. For IDH mutation, weighted averaging achieved an AUC of 0.799 ± 0.077 and a higher patient-level AUC than radiomics alone, whereas the comparison with meta-information alone was not statistically supported. Modality-group analyses revealed task-dependent performance patterns without identifying a consistently superior modality condition after multiplicity correction. Probability-level fusion showed task-dependent incremental discrimination and warrants further external and prospective evaluation with contemporary molecular reference standards and prespecified imaging harmonization procedures.

title: Beyond Segmentation: Coronary Artery Calcium Scoring with Frozen Self-Supervised CT Features.
abstract: Coronary artery calcium (CAC) scoring on computed tomography (CT) acquired for other indications could provide calcium-burden information without a dedicated scoring examination. We investigate direct, segmentation-free Agatston score prediction from frozen CT patch representations using only volume-level supervision for the scoring head. A lightweight additive head maps attention-selected features to non-negative contributions, combines them within slices, and sums slice scores across each volume. In developmental evaluation, applying the nonlinear mapping before aggregation improved linearly weighted κ by 0.27-0.38 over a pooled multilayer perceptron across six encoders. Using spatially adaptive label-guided temperature (SALT) features, held-out κ was 0.930 on gated CT and 0.844 on contrast-enhanced coronary CT angiography (CCTA), with separately fitted heads. On external non-gated CT, a head fitted on 165 patients from the same cohort achieved κ=0.727 on 40 held-out patients; patient-level five-fold cross-validation over all 205 patients yielded κ=0.639, indicating preliminary local-adaptation performance. Unchanged-head external gated transfer achieved κ=0.854 (n=443). Gated intraclass correlation coefficient ICC(A,1) on log(1+score) was 0.984. Study-level CAC scores served as CCTA reference targets; non-contrast images were not model inputs. SALT uses gated calcium masks during pretraining, not downstream scoring. Its highest-attention patch overlapped calcium in 89.5% of calcium-bearing slices, but localization rankings did not directly track scoring rankings. These results support direct, spatially decomposable CAC prediction from reusable features; broader validation is needed before clinical use.

title: Fine-Coarse Dual Multi-Scale Graph Convolutional Network with Adaptive Edge Construction for Classification and Survival Prediction of Whole-Slide Images.
abstract: Whole-slide images (WSIs) provide important morphological evidence for cancer diagnosis and prognostic assessment. However, their gigapixel size, substantial regional heterogeneity, complex spatial organization, and limited fine-grained annotations make it difficult to model the topological relationships among pathological regions, which in turn limits the use of WSI analysis in automated diagnosis and prognosis. We propose AECGCN, a fine-coarse dual multi-scale graph convolutional network with adaptive edge construction, for WSI classification and survival prediction. Patch-level features are first extracted using the pretrained CONCH (CONtrastive learning from Captions for Histopathology) model and compressed by MiniBatch K-Means clustering to construct fine- and coarse-grained graphs. Graph edges are then constructed adaptively by combining spatial distance with feature-based semantic similarity, where the relative weighting is calibrated by Moran's I spatial autocorrelation statistic, so that tissue topology and pathological relationships are captured jointly. Finally, two task-specific subnets, AECGCN-C for classification and AECGCN-S for survival prediction, integrate local pathological patterns and global tissue structure through dual-branch graph convolutions and cross-scale attention. Evaluated on datasets from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA), AECGCN achieves classification accuracy (ACC) values of 0.944±0.024 on the combined kidney cohort (TCGA-Kidney) and 0.914±0.027 on the breast invasive carcinoma cohort (TCGA-BRCA). For survival prediction, it achieves concordance index (C-index) values of 0.709±0.041 on the kidney renal clear cell carcinoma cohort (TCGA-KIRC) and 0.644±0.043 on TCGA-BRCA. The study provides a research-stage framework for image-based subtype classification and prognostic risk stratification with exploratory attention visualization. External validation, probability calibration, prospective evaluation, and human-in-the-loop review remain necessary before clinical use. Because the framework relies only on slide-level labels and generic patch-level features, the same fine-coarse dual graph design with adaptive edge construction can be extended to other clinical imaging applications and to other multi-scale or gigapixel image analysis tasks.

title: Synthesis and Application of a Chitosan-Based AM/AMPS Flocculant for the Flocculation of Kaolinite Suspensions: Experimental and Molecular Dynamics Study.
abstract: Fine kaolinite particles form stable suspensions that impede solid-liquid separation. A chitosan-based flocculant, CS-g-P(AM-AMPS), was synthesized by ultrasound-assisted graft copolymerization of acrylamide (AM) and 2-acrylamido-2-methylpropanesulfonic acid (AMPS) onto chitosan (CS). Physicochemical characterization, batch flocculation tests, and molecular dynamics simulations were conducted with the AM/AMPS copolymer P(AM-AMPS) and polyacrylamide (PAM) as reference polymers. Characterization identified amide and sulfonate groups and a rough, porous dry-state morphology. CS-g-P(AM-AMPS) achieved higher final turbidity removal and produced larger median flocs than both reference polymers under their respective selected conditions, with a maximum removal efficiency of 98.5%. Simulations showed that the grafted polymer had the most negative total polymer-surface interaction energy and the largest interfacial hydrogen-bond population. Its segment distribution combined near-surface enrichment with extension into the adjacent aqueous phase. P(AM-AMPS) produced larger median flocs than PAM but achieved lower removal, showing that aggregate size and clarification followed different rankings. These findings suggest that extensive surface contact coupled with chain extension facilitates particle bridging and floc growth. The combined results identify CS-g-P(AM-AMPS) as an effective flocculant for clarifying kaolinite-bearing water.

title: Cachexia Index and CRP-Triglyceride-Glucose Index as Prognostic Predictors in Cancer Hospitalized Patients.
abstract: Background/objectives Cancer cachexia is linked to poor oncological outcomes. The Cachexia Index (CXI) and the CRP-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), composite markers of body composition, nutrition, and inflammation, have emerged as prognostic tools, but their value in hospitalized cancer patients remains unexplored. We evaluated their association with short- and long-term outcomes in this population. Methods This retrospective, observational study included 139 hospitalized patients with active cancer by a Nutrition Unit during 2023. Nutritional status was assessed using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria; body composition was quantified by computed tomography (CT) imaging at L3 level. Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission due to clinical deterioration, hospital readmission, and overall survival. Each index was analyzed as a continuous variable, in quartiles, by the median, and at an exploratory ROC-derived cut-off, using logistic and Cox regression. Results CXI at its ROC-derived cut-off (<9.03; AUC 0.69) was associated with in-hospital mortality (OR 3.91; 95% CI 1.22-12.52; p = 0.022) and overall survival (HR 1.75; 95% CI 1.04-2.95; p = 0.035), unlike its continuous, quartile, and median forms. CTI at its cut-off (≥6.71; AUC 0.704) remained associated with ICU admission after adjustment for surgery and age (OR 5.52; 95% CI 1.64-18.54; p = 0.006) or surgery and myosteatosis (OR 4.94; 95% CI 1.48-16.47; p = 0.009), but not with survival. Conclusions CXI and CTI show complementary, threshold-dependent prognostic value: CXI identifies in-hospital and long-term mortality risk, and CTI, more consistently than CXI, identifies ICU admission risk due to clinical deterioration. These exploratory findings need prospective, multicenter validation.

Cancer cachexia is linked to poor oncological outcomes. The Cachexia Index (CXI) and the CRP-triglyceride-glucose index (CTI), composite markers of body composition, nutrition, and inflammation, have emerged as prognostic tools, but their value in hospitalized cancer patients remains unexplored. We evaluated their association with short- and long-term outcomes in this population.

Methods

This retrospective, observational study included 139 hospitalized patients with active cancer by a Nutrition Unit during 2023. Nutritional status was assessed using the Global Leadership Initiative on Malnutrition (GLIM) criteria; body composition was quantified by computed tomography (CT) imaging at L3 level. Primary outcomes were in-hospital mortality, intensive care unit (ICU) admission due to clinical deterioration, hospital readmission, and overall survival. Each index was analyzed as a continuous variable, in quartiles, by the median, and at an exploratory ROC-derived cut-off, using logistic and Cox regression.

Results

CXI at its ROC-derived cut-off (<9.03; AUC 0.69) was associated with in-hospital mortality (OR 3.91; 95% CI 1.22-12.52; p = 0.022) and overall survival (HR 1.75; 95% CI 1.04-2.95; p = 0.035), unlike its continuous, quartile, and median forms. CTI at its cut-off (≥6.71; AUC 0.704) remained associated with ICU admission after adjustment for surgery and age (OR 5.52; 95% CI 1.64-18.54; p = 0.006) or surgery and myosteatosis (OR 4.94; 95% CI 1.48-16.47; p = 0.009), but not with survival.

Conclusions

CXI and CTI show complementary, threshold-dependent prognostic value: CXI identifies in-hospital and long-term mortality risk, and CTI, more consistently than CXI, identifies ICU admission risk due to clinical deterioration. These exploratory findings need prospective, multicenter validation.

title: From Classification to Clinical Trust: 3D Deep Learning and Layer-Wise Explainability for Brain Tumor MRI.
abstract: Preoperative differentiation of glioma from meningioma on MRI is important for treatment planning but depends on expert interpretation. A 3D ResNet-34 with CBAM attention was trained on four-modality MRI from 2251 BraTS 2023 patients (1801 for four-fold cross-validation; 450 held out for testing) and achieved 96% accuracy, an AUC of 0.993, and an expected calibration error of 0.0165 on the test set. For layer-wise explanation, Grad-CAM and SmoothGrad were applied at the four residual stages, and a reconstruction decoder was added to obtain full-resolution, decoder-mediated attribution at the 4 × 4 × 4 bottleneck, where standard Grad-CAM is too coarse. Four quantitative metrics gave complementary results: the decoder-assisted attribution had the highest pointing-game accuracy (80.2%) and the lowest deletion AUC, whereas Layer 1 had the highest insertion AUC and Layer 2 the highest mean faithfulness delta, with no significant faithfulness difference among Layers 1, 2, and 4. Glioma was localized by most layers, while meningioma was localized mainly through the decoder-assisted pathway. A preliminary clinical review and a normalization analysis are also reported. The decoder offers an annotation-free way to obtain full-resolution attribution from deep layers of volumetric models.

title: Spatial Physics-Informed Neural Reconstruction for Ultrasound Travel-Time Tomography.
abstract: Ultrasound computed tomography provides speed-of-sound (SoS) images that complement conventional pulse-echo ultrasound, but estimating spatial acoustic structure from transmission data remains computationally demanding. We investigate a physics-informed learned reconstruction trained exclusively on synthetic SoS fields and Eikonal-calculated travel times. Diverse synthetic structures supply paired training data at scale, enabling learning without experimentally labeled SoS images. A supervised inverse, a latent image prior, and physics-conditioned corrections produce an image that can subsequently be refined through the Eikonal equation. Evaluation on held-out synthetic fields shows improved reconstruction relative to the supervised initial estimate, with further gains from post-inference physical refinement. Applied to ToFs extracted from an in vivo breast acquisition, the fixed learned models recover heterogeneous internal SoS structure, and refinement improves correspondence with an independent full-waveform-inversion reconstruction. Controlled analyses characterize the contributions of spatial conditioning and the dependence of reconstruction on timing, support, and numerical sampling. These findings demonstrate that synthetic structures can provide useful prior information for ultrasound travel-time reconstruction and establish the feasibility of combining rapid learned inference with image-specific physical refinement.

title: MRI Morphometry of the Pediatric Olfactory Bulb and Sulcus: Age-Related Changes and Reference Morphometric Values.
abstract: Background: Reference morphometric data for the olfactory sulcus (OS) and olfactory bulb (OB) in the pediatric population are scarce. This study aimed to evaluate the age-related morphometric characteristics of these structures using magnetic resonance imaging (MRI). Methods: This retrospective cross-sectional study included pediatric patients with normal brain MRI findings. Olfactory bulb diameters and olfactory sulcus depth were measured. Patients were grouped by age, and correlation, group comparison, and regression analyses were performed to evaluate associations with age. Results : A total of 248 children were enrolled. The mean olfactory bulb transverse and craniocaudal diameters were 2.69 ± 0.67 mm and 2.15 ± 0.65 mm on the right and 2.85 ± 0.71 mm and 2.25 ± 0.63 mm on the left, respectively. The mean olfactory sulcus depth was 10.08 ± 1.76 mm on the right and 9.72 ± 1.65 mm on the left. Sulcus depth showed a weak positive correlation with age (right: r = 0.277, p < 0.001; left: r = 0.259, p < 0.001), whereas bulb measurements demonstrated weaker associations (e.g., right bulb craniocaudal diameter: r = 0.153, p = 0.016). Quadratic regression analyses indicated that age significantly predicted sulcus depth (explaining 27.1% and 25.5% of the variance on the right and left sides, respectively, p < 0.001), whereas bulb measurements remained relatively stable. Conclusion: OB dimensions are relatively stable across childhood, whereas OS depth increases with age in the pediatric population. These data provide reference morphometric parameters to support the radiological evaluation of olfactory system development in children.

title: Pulmonary Artery CT Angiography on Photon-Counting Detector CT: A Practical One-Stop Acquisition, Reconstruction, and Reporting Protocol.
abstract: Background/objectives Computed tomography pulmonary angiography (CTPA) is the first-line test for suspected acute pulmonary embolism (PE), yet respiratory and cardiac motion artifacts, non-diagnostic opacification, subsegmental interpretive uncertainty, contrast medium and radiation dose burdens, and historically variable reporting persist. Photon-counting detector CT (PCCT), together with the newly released Pulmonary Embolism Reporting and Data System (PE-RADS) v2026, creates the opportunity for a standardized one-stop examination. This technical note consolidates the PCCT-CTPA evidence base into a practical acquisition, reconstruction, and reporting protocol. Methods The protocol was developed as a narrative, literature-informed synthesis of the PCCT-CTPA evidence base, identified by searching PubMed/MEDLINE, Scopus, and Web of Science from January 2021 (first clinical PCCT installation) to July 2026; sources included randomized and comparative clinical studies, phantom experiments, and a 2026 systematic review and meta-analysis pooling 12 studies and 950 patients. This technical note is not itself a systematic review, and pooled effect sizes are quoted from that existing meta-analysis rather than newly derived. Results The protocol specifies a sub-second (<1 s), free-breathing, dual-source high-pitch acquisition in QuantumPlus multi-energy mode, 25-40 mL of contrast medium as evidence-based example regimens rather than fixed volumes, routine reading on 50-55 keV virtual monoenergetic images (VMIs) with 40 keV bolus salvage and 90-120 keV streak suppression, iodine distribution (perfused-blood-volume surrogate) maps from the same scan at no additional dose, an optional ultra-high-resolution (UHR) problem-solving tier that replaces, rather than adds to, the standard acquisition in selected patients, and reporting aligned with PE-RADS v2026 categories, designations, and accessory findings. Effective doses of 1.3-1.4 mSv have been reported for low-dose PCCT protocols (including the free-breathing ultra-high-pitch protocol) under specified conditions; 89% of routine PCCT examinations were entirely artifact-free versus 28.6% on energy-integrating detector CT (EID-CT); and iodine maps diagnosed chronic thromboembolism with sensitivity 0.94 and specificity 0.84 at 1.3 mSv. Reported dose and contrast savings are protocol-dependent and did not retain meta-analytic significance after conservative adjustment. Conclusions PCCT enables an evidence-supported, PE-RADS-ready one-stop CTPA protocol delivering morphology and iodine-distribution (perfused-blood-volume surrogate) maps in every patient. It complements rather than replaces conventional CTPA, and local validation of dose, contrast use, and reporting outcomes is advised. Whether improved peripheral visibility translates into improved diagnostic accuracy for subsegmental PE remains unproven.

title: Evaluation of a Deep Learning Reconstruction Technique for Accelerated Brain MRI Scans.
abstract: Background/objectives Magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) is a cornerstone of diagnostic imaging, providing exceptional soft tissue contrast and enabling detailed characterization of neurological, vascular, and musculoskeletal diseases. Despite its clinical utility, prolonged acquisition times remain a primary limitation of MRI. Extended scan durations increase patient discomfort, particularly in vulnerable populations, which elevate the risk of motion artifacts that can degrade image quality and necessitate repeat imaging. Recent advances in machine learning, especially deep learning (DL), promise to ameliorate these limitations by enabling high-quality MRI reconstruction from heavily undersampled data, increasing throughput capacity and improving healthcare delivery efficiency. This work describes an FDA-cleared DL algorithm known as DeepFoqus-Accelerate for the reconstruction of deliberately under-sampled magnetic resonance imaging data. Methods Fully sampled k-space from 408 brain MRI volumes (108 from 18 healthy volunteers and 300 from the public fastMRI dataset) was retrospectively undersampled. A detailed comparison of reconstructed images using DeepFoqus-Accelerate with corresponding fully sampled clinical images is presented using expert evaluation of overall image quality and quantitative similarity metrics. The only conventional comparator included in the study was GE's parallel imaging reconstruction (ARC) at matched retrospective undersampling; comparisons with compressed sensing and vendor-specific deep-learning reconstruction methods were outside the study design. Results This algorithm can allow for a four-fold reduction in brain imaging times relative to a fully sampled acquisition while preserving image quality. No reader rated any reconstruction below the acceptability threshold, and DeepFoqus-Accelerate exceeded ARC on all metrics at 4×. Conclusions The findings characterize image quality and structural fidelity relative to fully sampled references and support further evaluation of diagnostic performance, with the potential to improve imaging efficiency and patient experience.

title: Pretreatment MRI Radiomics for Overall Survival Risk Stratification in Neuroendocrine Carcinoma of the Cervix: A Development and External Validation Study.
abstract: Background: Neuroendocrine carcinoma of the cervix (NECC) is a rare malignancy, and pretreatment overall survival (OS) assessment remains limited. We developed and externally validated an MRI radiomics model for OS risk stratification. Methods: This retrospective study included 128 patients: Center 1 served as the development cohort ( n = 90), and Center 2 as the independent external validation cohort ( n = 38). The model was selected using development data and locked before validation. Evaluation included Harrell C-index, inverse-probability-of-censoring-weighted (IPCW) AUC, calibration, Brier score, decision-curve analysis, and survival stratification. Results: The model comprised three intratumoral T2-weighted imaging features fitted using CoxBoost 1.5.2. Its external C-index was 0.737 (95% CI, 0.615-0.850), compared with 0.633 (95% CI, 0.523-0.749) for the revised clinical model; the paired difference was 0.104 (95% CI, -0.018 to 0.226). A nested sensitivity analysis of the automated selection procedure yielded a mean C-index of 0.592 (SD, 0.049). IPCW AUCs were 0.741 (95% CI, 0.562-0.891) at 3 years and 0.763 (95% CI, 0.583-0.919) at 5 years. At 3 and 5 years, calibration intercepts were 0.03 and -0.09, slopes 1.14 and 1.20, and Brier scores 0.202 and 0.195, respectively. Exploratory decision-curve analysis suggested potential net benefit over selected thresholds. Hazard ratios (HRs; 95% CIs) for high versus low risk were 1.96 (1.06-3.62) and 3.61 (1.39-9.38) in the development and external cohorts, respectively. Corresponding HRs per development-cohort SD increase in the score were 1.83 (1.29-2.60) and 2.42 (1.45-4.04). Conclusions: The pretreatment MRI radiomics model showed external prognostic discrimination for OS in NECC, but superiority over the pretreatment clinical model was not demonstrated. Further independent validation is needed.

title: AI-Driven CT Analysis for Aortic Disease: A Task-Based Systematic Review of Segmentation, Measurement, and Detection Applications.
abstract: Background/Objectives: Computed tomography (CT) and CT angiography (CTA) are central to assessing aortic aneurysm and dissection, but manual segmentation and geometric analysis remain time-consuming and operator-dependent, while evidence on artificial intelligence (AI) is fragmented. This task-based systematic review synthesised AI applications to CT/CTA of the thoracic and abdominal aorta by primary task: segmentation, measurement, or detection and classification. Methods: PubMed/MEDLINE and Europe PMC were searched from 2015 to September 2026 following PRISMA 2020; the protocol was registered retrospectively (INPLASY2026110004). Segmentation and measurement studies were appraised with CLAIM and detection studies with QUADAS-2/QUADAS-AI, and results were synthesised without meta-analysis. Results: Of 118 included studies (42 segmentation, 38 measurement, 38 detection), half were published since 2024. Median Dice similarity coefficient was 0.90 or higher for the outer wall, lumen and true and false lumina, but 0.86 for intraluminal thrombus and 0.63 for false lumen thrombus. Automated maximum diameter showed a median absolute bias of 0.26 mm (95% limits of agreement about ±5 mm). Detection of aortic dissection reached a median AUC of 0.96-0.97, mostly in enriched samples. External validation was reported in 14%, 34% and 55% of segmentation, measurement and detection studies, 33 of 38 detection studies were at high risk of bias, and only two systems were evaluated prospectively. Conclusions: AI supports technical automation of aortic CT/CTA segmentation and measurement and is progressing toward multistructure geometric phenotyping and clinical decision support, but independent multicentre validation, consecutive cohorts and prospective reader-in-the-loop studies are required before clinical integration. Detection/classification tools require independent diagnostic and workflow validation.

title: Longitudinal Retinal Layer Changes After Deep Sclerectomy in Primary Open-Angle Glaucoma: A Three-Year Retrospective Cohort Study Using Spectral-Domain OCT.
abstract: Background To evaluate longitudinal peripapillary and macular retinal layer changes over three years before and after deep sclerectomy (DS) in eyes with primary open-angle glaucoma (POAG). Methods This retrospective monocentric study included 150 eyes undergoing DS with intraoperative mitomycin C. Cohort 1 ( n = 111) was analyzed for absolute retinal layer thickness changes and cohort 2 ( n = 39) for pre- and postoperative thinning rates using spectral-domain OCT. Intraocular pressure (IOP), medication use, best-corrected visual acuity (BCVA), and visual field mean defect (MD) were assessed over three years. Results Mean IOP decreased significantly at three years in both cohorts (cohort 1: 22.8 ± 0.7 to 14.9 ± 0.7 mmHg; cohort 2: 20.8 ± 1.2 to 13.5 ± 0.9 mmHg; both p < 0.001), alongside a significant reduction in medication use ( p < 0.001). BCVA remained stable, whereas MD worsened significantly in a mixed-effects model (cohort 1: +0.70 dB/year, p = 0.002; cohort 2: +0.74 dB/year, p < 0.001). Despite sustained IOP reduction, mean peripapillary RNFL thickness declined (cohort 1: 60.1 ± 1.4 to 56.6 ± 1.8 µm, p < 0.001; cohort 2: 61.1 ± 2.4 to 57.4 ± 2.9 µm, p = 0.005). In cohort 2, the macular RNFL thinning rate decreased numerically after surgery (-1.40 ± 0.67 to -0.08 ± 0.47 µm/year; difference 1.32 µm/year, 95% CI -0.28 to 2.92; p = 0.11). Macular layers showed no significant changes. Conclusions DS achieved sustained IOP reduction with stable visual acuity, but visual field MD worsened over three years. Peripapillary RNFL thinning persisted postoperatively, though macular thinning rates showed a non-significant reduction. Structural monitoring remains necessary after glaucoma surgery despite adequate IOP control.

title: Temporal Waveform Reconstruction Algorithm for Fast Super-resolution Ultrasound Imaging.
abstract: Objective: A processing framework is introduced to address robustness and computational challenges in translating ultrasound localization microscopy (ULM), enabling fast and adaptive microvascular imaging. Impact Statement: Parameter-free filtering and accelerated localization triple processing speed provide a reliable foundation for real-time clinical super-resolution microvascular imaging. Introduction: ULM surpasses the acoustic diffraction limit to resolve microvasculature. However, its clinical adoption is hindered by parameter-sensitive filtering and computationally heavy localization and tracking. Methods: First, a parameter-free temporal waveform reconstruction filter adaptively recovers microbubble temporal signatures from raw time-series data, separating them from tissue clutter and operating 5.7 times faster than conventional filters. Second, a Gaussian fit radial symmetry method accelerates localization by adding a Gaussian similarity step to the standard local maximum radial symmetry approach, reducing processing time to one-third. Results: The workflow processes each frame in 0.0065 s, down from 0.02 s per frame, achieving a 3-fold speedup. It delivers 10-μm-scale super-resolution microvascular imaging validated on multiple public datasets. Conclusion: This efficient and adaptive framework markedly cuts ULM processing time, paving the way to real-time clinical microvascular imaging.

title: [Safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring filtered type-B transnasal specialized airway catheter in anesthesia for ambulatory gastrointestinal endoscopic surgery in obese patients].
abstract: Objective: To evaluate the clinical safety and efficacy of the adjustable monitoring and filtering type B transnasal specialized airway catheter (hereafter referred to as the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway) during anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy in obese patients. Methods: This randomized controlled trial enrolled 92 obese patients (body mass index≥28 kg/m²) scheduled for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under digestive endoscopy at the General Hospital of Northern Theater Command between June and December 2025. Using a random number table, we split the participants evenly into an adjustable airway group (Group R, n =46) and a standard nasal cannula group (Group C, n =46). Anesthesia was inducted and maintained with remimazolam and alfentanil. Patients in Group R were fitted with the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway for oxygen delivery and end-tidal carbon dioxide (etCO 2 ) monitoring, and Group C received supplemental oxygen through conventional nasal cannula. The primary outcome was defined as the incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia [pulse oximetry saturation(SpO 2 )<90%]. Secondary outcomes were the variations in respiratory rate, heart rate and mean arterial pressure (MAP) at time points before induction (T 0 ), upon endoscope insertion (T 1 ), 5 minutes post-insertion (T 2 ), at the end of surgery (T 3 ), and 5 minutes after waking up (T 4 ). Additional secondary outcomes included arterial partial pressure of oxygen (PaO₂) and arterial partial pressure of carbon dioxide (PaCO₂) at T 2 in both groups, and partial pressure of end-tidal carbon dioxide (PetCO₂) in group R. The duration of endoscopic therapy, dosages of remimazolam and alfentanil, the frequency of hands-on airway interventions, nasal bleeding episodes, and overall physician satisfaction scores were all systematically documented. Results: The baseline demographic and clinical characteristics matched up well between the two groups (all P >0.05). The incidence of intraoperative hypoxemia was significantly lower in group R compared with group C [2.2%(1/46) vs 32.6%(15/46), χ 2 =14.829, P <0.001]. Patients in Group R exhibited significantly elevated SpO 2 levels at T 1 , T 2 , and T 3 (all P <0.05). At T 2 , Group R demonstrated significantly higher PaO 2 and lower PaCO 2 compared to Group C, their heart rates also stayed distinctly lower ( P <0.05). MAP remained comparable across both cohorts at every measured interval ( P >0.05). Intraoperative PetCO 2 values in Group R were consistently maintained within normative physiological parameters, accompanied by continuous and stable monitoring waveforms. Compared with Group C, Group R registered a significantly lower rate of necessity for airway interventions, shorter endoscopic procedure duration and emergence time, lower remimazolam consumption, and highter physician satisfaction (all P <0.05). Conclusions: During anesthesia for elective ambulatory gastrointestinal polypectomy under gastrointestinal endoscopy in obese patients, the adjustable monitoring nasopharyngeal airway directly protects against hypoxemia by improving oxygen delivery and curtails carbon dioxide retention. Concurrently, accurate ventilation tracking helps maintain a highly stable hemodynamic profile, the clinical safety and efficacy of this airway device substantially surpass those of the conventional nasal cannula.

title: [Four cases of acute chemical lung injury induced by inhalation of nanocomposites].
abstract: Sprays Nanomaterial-containing may cause inhalational lung injury when used in confined spaces; However clinical evidence remains limited. We report four adult men who used sprays or coatings containing nano-titanium dioxide, a nanoscale fluoropolymer, or nano-silica in confined or poorly ventilated spaces without inadequate protection. All patients developed clinical manifestations such as chest tightness, cough, dyspnea, chest pain, or hemoptysis after exposure. Chest CT examinations revealed patchy or linear opacities, diffuse ground-glass opacities, or exudative changes. Some patients also had increased white bloodcell and neutrophil counts and C-reactive protein levels. Based on exposure history, imaging, toxicological testing, resutts, and exclusion of alternative causes, the diagnoses of acute chemical lung injury or nanocomposite-related poisoning were considered. The patients were treated with measures including removal from exposure, oxygen therapy or symptomatic supportive care, glucocorticoids, and anti-infective therapy. One patient underwent bronchoscopic bronchoalveolar lavage. Cases 3 and 4 showed clinical and radiographic improvement within a short period and were discharged, while cases 1 and 2 had persistent chest tightness, hemoptysis, or reduced exercise tolerance after delayed presentation. Clinicians should actively inquire about confined-space exposure to nanomaterial sprays or renovation products in patients with otherwise unexplained acute respiratory symptoms. Early identification and intervention are sessential to improve the prognosis of patients.

title: [Advances in pathologic diagnosis and updates in classification and grading of pleural mesothelioma].
abstract: Pleural mesothelioma (PMe) is a primary malignant tumor originating from pleural mesothelial cells, characterized by high invasiveness, rapid progression and poor prognosis. Its occurrence closely associated with asbestos exposure. The diagnosis of pleural mesothelioma presents several challenges in diagnostic pathology, as each histological subtype has its own unique differential diagnosis. No single antibody is completely sensitive or specific for mesothelioma; instead, the diagnosis relies on a combination of several antibody panels. The most commonly mutated genes in pleural mesothelioma are BAP1 , CDKN2A , and NF2 .Accurate diagnosis and evaluation of pleural mesothelioma typically require a multimodal approach, combining cytological testing, CT scans, and MRI imaging. This article comprehensive reviews the pathological diagnosis and differential diagnosis of PMe, interprets the relevant updates in the 2021 WHO classification of thoracic tumors. It synthesizes and summarizes the clinicopathological features of pleural mesothelioma, including the main differential diagnoses, diagnostic pitfalls, and criteria for distinguishing benign from malignant lesions. Furthermore, the article reviews the latest advancements in molecular genetic research on mesothelioma, exploring the involved pathogenesis and diagnostic methods. It also reviews the prognostic indicators associated with this disease. By providing these insights, the article offers valuable guidance for both the pathological diagnosis and clinical management of mesothelioma.

title: A Repeatable CT-Based Protocol for Nasal Cavity Volumetry and Choanal Airway Classification in Pediatric Syndromic Craniosynostosis.
abstract: Syndromic craniosynostosis (SC), such as Apert and Crouzon syndromes, causes midface hypoplasia that severely limits nasal cavity development. A computed tomography (CT)-based volumetric protocol for nasal cavity volumetry and choanal airway classification in pediatric SC patients, using landmark-based image segmentation software, is described and tested for intra-rater reproducibility. The protocol was applied to 10 SC patients (5 Apert, 5 Crouzon; 2-48 months; paired pre-/postoperative CT) and 10 reference children (60-168 months), not age-matched because CT is rarely indicated in healthy children. Intra-rater reliability was excellent (ICC = 0.987 and 0.909; 95% CI 0.934-0.997 and 0.689-0.976). Preoperative nasal cavity volume was significantly lower in SC patients (median 2,063.77 mm 3 ; Q1-Q3 1,275.53-3,457.18) than in the reference group (median 35,502.13 mm 3 ; Q1-Q3 28,811.21-39,167.15) (Mann-Whitney U = 0.000, Z = -3.780, p < 0.001). Nasal cavity volume increased between the paired CT scans in nine of ten patients (Wilcoxon Z = -2.701, p = 0.007; difference in medians +1,584.25 mm 3 ; +76.8%), remaining at only 10.3% of the reference group median postoperatively. A weighted regression sensitivity analysis (log[Volume] vs log[Age], w = 1/Age; n = 10), accounting for the age disparity between cohorts, yielded an exploratory, model-based, non-normative estimate of 7,580 mm 3 at the SC median age (8.5 months), extrapolated below the reference group age range; the SC median represented 27.2% of this estimate. Preoperative volume varied descriptively by choanal category (normal, stenosis, atresia) without tracking narrowing severity, possibly reflecting global hypoplasia; small subgroups precluded inferential testing. Nasal cavity volume is an anatomical measure and does not by itself indicate functional airway obstruction. The protocol offers a standardized workflow for larger, age-matched multicenter studies.

title: Candidate Magnetic Resonance Imaging Biomarkers of Language Recovery in Post-Stroke Aphasia: A Framework for Future Acupuncture-Response Prediction.
abstract: Language recovery after post-stroke aphasia (PSA) shows substantial interindividual variability, creating a need for objective markers that can characterize recovery potential and support individualized rehabilitation. This narrative review synthesizes magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) evidence relevant to language recovery and rehabilitation response in PSA, including structural MRI, diffusion MRI, functional MRI, and multimodal imaging. Existing studies indicate that lesion characteristics, white-matter integrity, regional functional activity, functional connectivity, and dynamic network organization are associated with aphasia severity, subsequent language recovery, or response to conventional rehabilitation. Multimodal approaches integrating imaging with clinical and behavioral information may provide a more comprehensive representation of individual recovery potential. Given the growing interest in applying neuroimaging to individualized acupuncture rehabilitation for PSA, an important question is whether these recovery-related MRI features can also inform acupuncture-response prediction. However, these findings primarily concern general prognosis or conventional rehabilitation outcomes and should not be interpreted as evidence of acupuncture-specific responsiveness. Acupuncture-related neuroimaging studies have mainly characterized treatment-associated changes in brain activity and functional connectivity rather than prospectively testing whether pretreatment MRI features predict individual treatment response. Accordingly, these MRI findings are better regarded as candidate imaging features for future acupuncture-response research than as validated predictors of acupuncture-specific benefit. We therefore propose a hypothesis-driven framework in which multimodal MRI is integrated with clinical and treatment information and evaluated within prospective controlled designs to distinguish general recovery potential from additional benefit attributable to acupuncture. Rigorous model development, external validation, and prospective testing will be required before imaging-based approaches can be considered for individualized acupuncture-response stratification.

title: The Effect of Alzheimer's Disease and Diabetes on the Volume of Brain Structures.
abstract: Alzheimer's disease (AD) and diabetes mellitus (DM) are increasingly prevalent chronic disorders with overlapping effects on brain structure. However, direct volumetric comparisons among patients with AD alone, DM alone, both conditions, and healthy controls remain limited. This retrospective study compared regional brain volumes in 160 adults (18-90 years) assigned equally to four groups (n = 40 each): AD+type 1 DM, AD-only, type 1 DM-only, and healthy controls. Brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) scans were analyzed using VolBrain, an automated, multiatlas, patch-based segmentation platform, on 3D T1-weighted magnetization-prepared rapid gradient-echo (MPRAGE) images acquired at 1.5 T. Regions evaluated included white and gray matter, subcortical structures, selected cortical gyri, and the ventricular system. Analyses were stratified by sex. No significant volumetric differences were observed between the AD+DM and AD-only groups. Compared with DM-only, differences were limited to the right amygdala (p = 0.004) and left thalamus (p = 0.001) in females. Relative to controls, both AD groups showed reductions in the bilateral amygdala, bilateral caudate, right thalamus, and middle temporal gyrus, together with third-ventricle enlargement (all p ≤ 0.005). The DM-only group showed fewer abnormalities. Reduced left caudate volume was the only finding consistently observed across all patient groups and both sexes (p ≤ 0.007). Overall, AD and DM showed partially overlapping regional differences in brain volume. The consistent left caudate reduction may represent a shared structural marker and warrants further prospective and longitudinal investigation in AD-DM comorbidity.

title: Percutaneous Transhepatic Cholangioscopy: Technical Evolution and Expanding Clinical Roles.
abstract: Percutaneous transhepatic cholangioscopy (PTCS) has evolved from a niche diagnostic technique into an increasingly versatile platform for managing complex biliary diseases, particularly in patients with surgically altered anatomy or failed conventional endoscopic access. Early applications were limited by suboptimal visualization, rigid instrumentation, and procedural complexity. Refinements in endoscopic design and percutaneous techniques now support direct intraductal visualization and targeted intervention through a transhepatic tract. Recent developments include digital single-operator systems, scope miniaturization, and dedicated therapeutic accessories. These advances facilitate targeted biopsy and lithotripsy, although comparative evidence for improved diagnostic accuracy, safety, or patient-centered outcomes remains limited. Relevant literature was identified through a targeted PubMed/MEDLINE search through October 17, 2026, and reference-list screening, with bibliographic verification in Crossref. This narrative review distinguishes PTCS-specific evidence from peroral and mixed-access cholangioscopy studies and summarizes representative clinical outcomes. Technical success, diagnostic yield, malignancy-discrimination accuracy, and therapeutic success are considered separately. The review also addresses collaboration with interventional radiology, access selection, staged versus single-session procedures, drainage management, and alternative treatment pathways. Existing evidence remains heterogeneous in procedural indications, outcome definitions, adverse-event reporting, and device generations. Three-dimensional reconstruction has limited comparative clinical data, whereas the cited artificial intelligence application is a peroral feasibility report without established PTCS benefit. This synthesis aims to clarify the current role of PTCS in hepatobiliary practice and identify priorities for technique standardization, safety reporting, and prospective comparative validation.

title: Host Fitness in Gastrointestinal Oncology: Beyond Tumor Biology.
abstract: Patients with gastrointestinal cancers face site-specific threats to nutritional intake, muscle function, organ reserve, and recovery. This critical narrative review examines host fitness as an organizing concept for these vulnerabilities rather than as a validated composite score. A targeted PubMed update identified publications from 2022 through September 14, 2026, using gastrointestinal cancer terms combined with prehabilitation, microbiome-immunotherapy, geriatric assessment, exercise, and digital assessment terms, while retaining relevant foundational studies. The review distinguishes guideline-supported care from prognostic associations and research-stage applications. Geriatric and nutritional assessments can guide established supportive care, whereas computed tomography-derived body composition and inflammatory indices primarily provide prognostic information. Microbiome signatures, epigenetic clocks, and integrated digital models require further validation before they can guide treatment decisions. Intervention effects vary by tumor site and treatment phase: selected prehabilitation trials demonstrate short-term benefits, although findings remain inconsistent, while long-term exercise after adjuvant chemotherapy for colon cancer represents a distinct evidence base. An operational assessment protocol and multidisciplinary workflow are presented to link documented impairments with existing care pathways and repeated assessment. No host-fitness threshold is proposed for treatment escalation, de-escalation, or sequencing. Prospective studies should establish incremental predictive value and patient benefit beyond existing assessments before this integrated framework is used to support precision treatment decisions.

title: Optimized Tissue Microarray for In Situ Characterization of Central Nervous System Tumors Using a Spatial Transcriptomics Platform.
abstract: We present a standardized, end-to-end development and application of a Xenium tissue microarray (TMA) to profile glioblastoma, meningioma, schwannomas, and pituitary neuroendocrine tumors (PitNETs). The workflow covers: (i) pathology-guided selection of representative tumor regions (including tumor core and immune-rich interfaces when available); (ii) core extraction and array design to balance patient groups and clinical timepoints within each block; (iii) TMA embedding, sectioning, and slide preparation compatible with Xenium chemistry; (iv) assay execution, imaging, transcript decoding, and cell segmentation. This high-throughput workflow is specific for generating TMAs optimized for Xenium in situ spatial transcriptomics for different central nervous system (CNS) tumor types. Spatial profiling of CNS tumors in focused studies (i.e., clinical trials) is often limited by scarce tissue, heterogeneity across tumor regions, and batch effects introduced by processing specimens across multiple runs. Building a Xenium-compatible TMA enables uniform handling of many patient samples and time points on a single slide, thereby improving cross-sample consistency while reducing reagent cost and turnaround time. We also highlight practical troubleshooting steps encountered in tumor sections, such as tissue loss and segmentation artifacts in highly cellular or necrotic regions. Representative results are summarized using key assay quality metrics to assess performance across cores, including usable tissue area, numbers of segmented cells/nuclei per core, decoded transcript yield, genes detected per cell, and the fraction of transcripts assigned to cells. This protocol yields reproducible, cell-resolved spatial gene expression maps across multiple tumor regions in parallel, enabling direct comparison of naïve and recurrent disease within a therapeutic context. This TMA approach is broadly applicable to both untreated and treated biospecimens, where standardized processing and scalable spatial profiling are essential for biomarker discovery and mechanistic insight.

title: Diagnostic Reasoning and Staged Surgery for Culture-Negative Foot Infection Molecularly Suggestive of Mycobacterium fortuitum: A Case Report.
abstract: Post-traumatic infections caused by rapidly growing nontuberculous mycobacteria can be difficult to diagnose because clinical findings are nonspecific and conventional microbiological studies may be negative. This case describes a 15-year-old previously healthy male with a non-healing left-foot wound and intermittent fever after injury with a farm tool. Targeted next-generation sequencing of soft tissue at an outside hospital suggested Mycobacterium fortuitum, with 1296 sequence reads. Magnetic resonance imaging demonstrated a deep infectious lesion with abscess cavity formation, and radiography suggested fifth metatarsal involvement. After admission, inflammatory markers remained elevated; however, acid-fast staining, mycobacterial deoxyribonucleic acid (DNA) testing, 42-day mycobacterial culture, and anaerobic culture were negative. Empirical combination antimicrobial therapy targeting nontuberculous mycobacteria was initiated. Because of extensive soft-tissue infection and suspected osteomyelitis, treatment was performed in stages. First-stage debridement and dead-space management were undertaken on July 2, 2025, followed by continued antimicrobial therapy. After improvement of local inflammation, second-stage surgery on November 5, 2025 removed residual metatarsal lesions and abnormal tissue. The wound was stable at discharge, and oral faropenem was continued. Long-term outcome could not be assessed because the patient was lost to follow-up. The case emphasizes integrating exposure history, imaging, intraoperative findings, molecular testing, and deep microbiological sampling when post-traumatic rapidly growing mycobacterial infection is suspected.

title: A Reproducible Two-Session Ultrasound-Guided Radiofrequency Ablation Protocol for Dialysis-Associated Secondary Hyperparathyroidism.
abstract: Secondary hyperparathyroidism (SHPT) is a common and clinically important complication in dialysis patients, and a subset of patients remains refractory to medical therapy or is unsuitable for surgery. Ultrasound-guided radiofrequency ablation (RFA) has emerged as a minimally invasive image-guided treatment option for selected patients with enlarged parathyroid glands. This Methods Article describes a reproducible two-session protocol for treating multiple hyperplastic parathyroid glands under real-time ultrasound guidance. The protocol includes patient selection, biochemical and ultrasound evaluation, gland numbering, staged session planning, protective hydrodissection, in-plane electrode control, moving-shot ablation, immediate endpoint assessment, inter-session reassessment, and dialysis-specific calcium monitoring. Representative results from 20 dialysis patients show that the protocol can be implemented with rapid reduction of intact parathyroid hormone (iPTH) and a need for active post-ablation calcium surveillance. The article is intended to provide a detailed procedural framework for centers developing staged ultrasound-guided parathyroid RFA rather than to establish superiority over parathyroidectomy or single-session ablation.

title: PET/CT Radiomics and Clinical Features for Classifying Transcriptome-Defined Immune Subgroups in Non-Small Cell Lung Cancer: A Retrospective Study.
abstract: Tumor immune phenotypes are clinically relevant in non-small cell lung cancer (NSCLC), but tissue-based assessment is invasive and vulnerable to sampling bias. This retrospective observational study evaluated whether positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) radiomic features combined with clinical variables could classify transcriptome-defined immune subgroups. Data from 184 patients were analyzed between January 2021 and December 2024 and used a computer-generated stratified 7:3 split to form a modeling cohort (n = 129) and an internal validation cohort (n = 55). Consensus clustering of transcriptomic profiles defined two immune subgroups. After reproducibility filtering, minimum redundancy maximum relevance analysis and least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression retained six radiomic features. The final combined model included the radiomic score, smoking history, pathological type, and pleural adhesion. The combined model achieved an area under the receiver operating characteristic curve (AUC) of 0.841 (95% confidence interval [CI], 0.772-0.909) in the modeling cohort and 0.822 (95% CI = 0.712-0.932) in the validation cohort. Compared with the radiomics-only model, the AUC gain was significant in the modeling cohort (p = 0.014) but not in the validation cohort (p = 0.590). At the modeling-derived threshold of 0.502, sensitivity and specificity were 76.5% and 82.0% in the modeling cohort and 75.9% and 69.2% in the validation cohort. Calibration intercepts and slopes were approximately 0 and 1.000 in the modeling cohort and -0.229 and 1.310 in the validation cohort. These findings support an internally evaluated association between routine PET/CT phenotypes and transcriptome-defined immune subgroups, but external validation and recalibration are required before clinical use.

title: Application of Explainable Machine Learning for Individualized Risk Stratification and Surgical Optimization in Geriatric Intertrochanteric Fractures.
abstract: Mechanical failure remains a critical complication in the fixation of intertrochanteric fractures. While the Tip-Apex Distance (TAD) is a well-established prognostic metric, the independent biomechanical impact of the nail entry point remains controversial due to confounding surgical variables. This study aimed to evaluate the stability offered by a medialized entry point using interpretable machine learning. A retrospective cohort of 628 patients treated with cephalomedullary nailing was analyzed. A Random Forest model was developed using 12 clinical and radiographic variables to predict implant failure. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) were used to disentangle confounding factors and visualize non-linear interactions between the entry-point strategy and TAD. The medialized entry point group exhibited a significantly lower failure rate compared to the standard group (25.3% vs. 44.2%; p < 0.001). The predictive model demonstrated robust performance (AUC: 0.877) on an independent testing set. Crucially, SHAP interaction analysis revealed a "buffering" effect: while risk profiles were comparable at optimal TAD levels, the medialized trajectory significantly attenuated the probability of failure when the TAD exceeded 25 mm, potentially mitigating the increased risk associated with suboptimal screw placement. The findings identify the medialized entry point as a significant independent predictor of success, increasing the biomechanical tolerance of the fixation construct. This surgical modification offers a valuable safety margin, particularly in cases where anatomical reduction or ideal screw positioning is challenging.
