title: A Digital Clinician-Technician Collaborative Workflow for Complete-Arch Implant Rehabilitation in Edentulous Patients.
abstract: This case report describes a digital clinician-technician collaborative workflow for complete-arch implant rehabilitation in a 70-year-old woman with severe periodontitis and compromised dentition. The workflow integrated clinical examination, cone-beam computed tomography, intraoral and facial scanning, mandibular movement records, virtual treatment planning, guided implant placement, and computer-aided design/computer-aided manufacturing. Digital data sharing facilitated communication between the clinician and dental technician throughout surgical and prosthetic procedures. Following the extraction of compromised teeth, implants were placed using digitally designed surgical guides, and implant positions were recorded with scan bodies to fabricate an immediate provisional restoration. After six months, a definitive one-piece all-ceramic implant-supported prosthesis was digitally designed and fabricated. Clinical assessment demonstrated a stable prosthetic fit, acceptable occlusion, and no major complications during follow-up. This case illustrates a reproducible, digitally coordinated approach to integrating clinical and laboratory procedures in complete-arch implant rehabilitation, while acknowledging the limitations inherent in a single-patient case report and the need for further clinical validation.

title: A CT-Based Radiomic Nomogram for Predicting FAM160A1 Expression and Survival in Ovarian Cancer.
abstract: Ovarian cancer (OC) has a poor prognosis due to late diagnosis and tumor heterogeneity. Noninvasive biomarkers for guiding individualized treatment remain limited. FAM160A1 has emerged as a potential prognostic gene in OC, but its expression requires tissue sampling. This study aimed to develop and validate a contrast-enhanced computed tomography (CT)-based radiomic model for the non-invasive prediction of FAM160A1 expression and to evaluate its prognostic value for overall survival (OS) in patients with OC. Transcriptomic, contrast-enhanced CT, and clinicopathological data were obtained from The Cancer Genome Atlas (TCGA) and The Cancer Imaging Archive (TCIA). FAM160A1 expression was associated with survival in Cox regression. Radiomic features were extracted from CT images, selected using least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) regression with 10-fold cross-validation repeated 1,000 times, and used to construct a logistic regression model. High FAM160A1 expression was significantly associated with reduced OS in univariable analysis (HR = 1.41, 95% CI: 1.09-1.81, P = 0.008); after multivariable adjustment, the point estimate was attenuated and no longer statistically significant (HR = 1.23, 95% CI: 0.94-1.60, P = 0.13). The radiomic model predicted FAM160A1 expression with areas under the ROC curve (AUCs) of 0.830 in the training set and 0.704 under internal cross-validation. A nomogram combining the radiomic score with clinical factors predicted 60-month OS with an AUC of 0.735, and DCA indicated a net benefit over treat-all and treat-none strategies only within an intermediate range of threshold probabilities. Subgroup analysis suggested that the prognostic effect of FAM160A1 was modified by age and chemotherapy. The CT-based radiomic model can predict FAM160A1 expression and survival outcomes in OC and offers a non-invasive tool to inform individualized prognosis and treatment planning, supporting the integration of radiomics into precision oncology for OC patients; confirmation in independent, prospectively collected cohorts is required before clinical use.​.

title: Single-Stage Lower Eyelid Reconstruction with Free Tarsoconjunctival Graft, Periosteal Flap, and Tripier Flap After Basal Cell Carcinoma Excision.
abstract: Basal cell carcinoma is the most common malignancy of the periocular region, and the lower eyelid is the site most frequently involved. Full-thickness excision of lower eyelid tumors that extend laterally often removes the lateral tarsus and canthal support, producing defects that cannot be closed directly. Reconstruction must then restore the posterior lamella, the anterior lamella, and lateral canthal fixation, and at least one lamella must carry its own blood supply. The goal of this protocol is to describe a single-stage reconstruction that avoids the temporary eyelid occlusion required by two-stage techniques. The tumor is excised full-thickness with a 5 mm clinical margin, and the wound edges are cauterized and released. A periosteal flap raised from the lateral orbital rim is used as a hammock for lateral fixation. A free tarsoconjunctival graft harvested from the ipsilateral upper eyelid is sutured to the remaining lower eyelid margin and to the periosteal flap with 6-0 polyglactin 910, and a lateral canthopexy is performed with 5-0 polypropylene. The anterior lamella is rebuilt with a pedicled Tripier myocutaneous flap of redundant upper eyelid skin and orbicularis oculi muscle, which provides the vascular bed for the graft, and the donor site is closed with 6-0 polypropylene. The protocol is illustrated in an 84-year-old woman with a 3-year history of a growing pigmented lesion of the left lower eyelid. Histopathology showed an ulcerated basal cell carcinoma of solid and adenoid type with tumor at the nasal surgical margin, which was managed with topical imiquimod 5%. Because the eyelid is a high-risk site, intraoperative margin control before reconstruction is advisable whenever it is available.

title: Adjunctive Fibular Shortening Osteotomy During Total Ankle Arthroplasty for Severe Varus Ankle Osteoarthritis: A Retrospective Case Series.
abstract: Background Severe varus ankle osteoarthritis can make total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) technically difficult because residual coronal malalignment, lateral gutter impingement, and unstable talar reduction may persist despite standard bone preparation and soft-tissue balancing. This study describes early clinical and radiographic outcomes after adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy in a highly selected subgroup of patients undergoing TAA for severe varus ankle osteoarthritis. Materials and methods We retrospectively reviewed 4 patients who underwent adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy during TAA after standard intraoperative balancing failed to restore stable talar reduction and adequate lateral clearance. These cases were identified from 320 TAAs performed over a 10-year period. Radiographic assessment included talocrural angle difference relative to the contralateral ankle and fibular length discrepancy. Clinical assessments included the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score and 36-item Short Form (SF-36) survey. Descriptive statistics were used. Results All 4 ankles had severe varus deformity >30° and preoperative talocrural angle difference >7° compared with the contra-lateral ankle. Mean fibular shortening was 8.2 ± 0.9 mm. Mean talocrural angle difference improved from 9.2° ± 1.3° preoperatively to 0.6° ± 0.3° postoperatively. Fibular union occurred in all cases at a mean of approximately 20 weeks. The mean AOFAS ankle-hindfoot score improved from 38.8 ± 3.0 to 54.2 ± 1.7, and the mean SF-36 score improved from 26.5 ± 1.9 to 42.2 ± 3.1. No fixation failure or recurrent gross instability was observed during follow-up. Conclusion Adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy may be considered as a selective intraoperative balancing option during TAA for severe varus ankle osteoarthritis when residual lateral impingement and instability persist after standard bone preparation and soft-tissue balancing. Larger studies with validated patient-reported outcomes and longer follow-up are required to define its indications and durability.
originalAbstract:
Background

Severe varus ankle osteoarthritis can make total ankle arthroplasty (TAA) technically difficult because residual coronal malalignment, lateral gutter impingement, and unstable talar reduction may persist despite standard bone preparation and soft-tissue balancing. This study describes early clinical and radiographic outcomes after adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy in a highly selected subgroup of patients undergoing TAA for severe varus ankle osteoarthritis.

Materials and methods

We retrospectively reviewed 4 patients who underwent adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy during TAA after standard intraoperative balancing failed to restore stable talar reduction and adequate lateral clearance. These cases were identified from 320 TAAs performed over a 10-year period. Radiographic assessment included talocrural angle difference relative to the contralateral ankle and fibular length discrepancy. Clinical assessments included the American Orthopaedic Foot & Ankle Society (AOFAS) ankle-hindfoot score and 36-item Short Form (SF-36) survey. Descriptive statistics were used.

Results

All 4 ankles had severe varus deformity >30° and preoperative talocrural angle difference >7° compared with the contra-lateral ankle. Mean fibular shortening was 8.2 ± 0.9 mm. Mean talocrural angle difference improved from 9.2° ± 1.3° preoperatively to 0.6° ± 0.3° postoperatively. Fibular union occurred in all cases at a mean of approximately 20 weeks. The mean AOFAS ankle-hindfoot score improved from 38.8 ± 3.0 to 54.2 ± 1.7, and the mean SF-36 score improved from 26.5 ± 1.9 to 42.2 ± 3.1. No fixation failure or recurrent gross instability was observed during follow-up.

Conclusion

Adjunctive fibular shortening osteotomy may be considered as a selective intraoperative balancing option during TAA for severe varus ankle osteoarthritis when residual lateral impingement and instability persist after standard bone preparation and soft-tissue balancing. Larger studies with validated patient-reported outcomes and longer follow-up are required to define its indications and durability.

title: Use of an Artificial Intelligence Model for Automated Measurement of the Anterior Segment by Ultrasound Biomicroscopy in ICL Calculation.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the agreement between an artificial intelligence-based automated system and manual ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) measurements of anterior segment parameters relevant to Implantable Collamer Lens (ICL; STAAR Surgical) planning. Methods This cross-sectional, observational, and analytical study was conducted at a tertiary referral ophthalmology center in Mexico City, Mexico. A total of 400 ultrasound biomicroscopy images of the anterior segment corresponding to one image per patient were used to generate segmentation masks and train a U-Net-based automated measurement model. An independent test dataset consisting of 40 UBM images from 40 different patients, not included in the training dataset, was used for model evaluation. Dataset splitting was performed at the patient level to avoid data leakage. Automated measurements of anterior chamber depth (ACD), angle-to-angle distance (ATA), sulcus-to-sulcus distance (STS), ciliary body inner diameter (CBID), and sulcus-to-sulcus lens rise (SSLR) were compared with manual measurements performed by an experienced ocular ultrasonographer. Results Automated measurements showed good to excellent agreement with manual measurements for ACD, ATA, STS, and CBID (intraclass correlation coefficient [ICC]: 0.891 to 0.994). In contrast, SSLR demonstrated moderate agreement (ICC: 0.680 to 0.810). Bland-Altman analysis showed minimal bias and no evidence of proportional error across parameters. Conclusions The artificial intelligence model demonstrated good agreement with manual measurements for most anterior segment parameters, with variable performance across parameters. These findings support the potential role of automated UBM-based measurements as an adjunctive tool for anatomical assessment in ICL planning. Further studies are warranted to determine its impact on ICL sizing decisions and postoperative outcomes.

title: Artificial Intelligence in Pediatric Hospital Medicine: Foundations, Clinical Applications, and Emerging Case Uses.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is rapidly transforming health care and has important implications for pediatric hospital medicine. Advances in machine learning and large language models have enabled applications that support patient care in the areas of clinical documentation, decision making, and prognostic modeling. Pediatric AI systems leverage diverse data sources, including electronic health records, medical imaging, physiologic monitoring, wearable devices, and genomic data. Current applications include AI-powered scribes, chart summarization, clinical decision support, prediction of sepsis and clinical deterioration, precision pharmacotherapy, rare disease diagnosis, and mental health interventions. These technologies have demonstrated potential to reduce clinician workload, enhance diagnostic accuracy, and facilitate earlier therapeutic interventions. However, significant challenges remain, including limited and heterogeneous pediatric datasets by virtue of age and developmental characteristics in children, bias, privacy concerns, lack of representativeness, and the need for rigorous validation and oversight. As AI adoption expands, pediatric hospitalists require foundational knowledge of AI principles and limitations to ensure safe, equitable, and effective implementation. With appropriate governance and multidisciplinary collaboration, AI has the potential to improve pediatric inpatient outcomes and health care delivery.

title: Ultrasound Biomicroscopic Features of Ciliary Epithelial Detachment in Bilateral Hypotony: A Novel Diagnosis.
abstract: The purpose of this study was to describe the clinical and ultrasound biomicroscopy (UBM) features of a previously unreported entity, ciliary epithelial detachment, in a patient with metastatic melanoma treated with nivolumab and presenting with bilateral hypotony. Visual acuity was 0.6 logMAR in the right eye and 1.3 logMAR in the left, with intraocular pressures of 7 mmHg in the right eye and 5 mmHg in the left. UBM revealed abnormal ciliary body morphology with truncation of ciliary processes and a distinct separation at the level of the ciliary epithelium in both eyes, most prominent inferotemporally. No evidence of fibrovascular proliferation or tractional distortion suggestive of cyclitic membrane was identified. These findings suggest a novel imaging phenotype: a ciliary epithelial detachment. Recognition of this entity may improve interpretation of anterior segment imaging in hypotony and refine diagnostic classification of ciliary body pathology.

title: Carcinoma in situ of the upper urinary tract: a scoping review mapping the evidence and research gaps.
abstract: Background Carcinoma in situ (CIS) of the upper urinary tract (UUT) is a rare, highgrade, non-invasive urothelial neoplasm whose diagnostic and therapeutic management remains largely extrapolated from bladder CIS. No comprehensive update of the evidence has been produced since the landmark consensus review of 2017. Objective To systematically map the breadth, nature and gaps of the available literature on UUT-CIS, using the Population- Concept-Context (PCC) framework, focusing on diagnosis, treatment, molecular/genetic characterization and prognosis. Methods This scoping review followed the Arksey and O'Malley framework and was reported according to the PRISMA extension for Scoping Reviews (PRISMA-ScR). PubMed/MEDLINE, Embase, Scopus, Web of Science and the Cochrane Library were searched from January 2000 through September 2026, supplemented by guideline repositories and hand-searching of reference lists. Because scoping reviews are not eligible for PROSPERO registration, the protocol was defined a priori but not prospectively registered in a public repository; this is acknowledged as a limitation. Results Of 643 records identified, 36 sources were retained for narrative synthesis, including 28 primary or empirical studies. Computed tomography urography shows high sensitivity (92%) but poor detection of flat lesions; urinary cytology and ureteroscopic biopsy remain the diagnostic mainstays despite limited sensitivity and sampling constraints. Kidney-sparing topical therapy (bacillus Calmette-Guérin [BCG] or mitomycin reversethermal gel) achieves complete response in 59-100% of cases but with highly heterogeneous recurrence (0-70%) and progression (0-43%) rates, reflecting the absence of standardized delivery protocols. Mismatch-repair protein loss and Lynch syndrome are identified in up to 9-14% of cases, supporting universal reflex screening. Concomitant CIS is consistently reported as an independent predictor of worse recurrence-free and cancer-specific survival after radical nephroureterectomy. Conclusions Evidence on UUT-CIS remains fragmented, predominantly retrospective and single-institutional. Five priority research gaps were identified: absence of a standardized histological/ imaging definition, lack of standardized topical-therapy protocols, scarcity of prospective long-term data, near-absence of quality-of-life/patient-reported outcomes, and underuse of molecular risk stratification. Multi-institutional prospective registries are needed to inform future evidence-based guidelines.

title: Correlation of Spectral Doppler Indices of Superior Thyroid Artery and Apparent Diffusion Coefficient Values in Benign and Malignant Thyroid Nodules in a Tertiary Level Hospital.
abstract: Background Thyroid nodules are common in clinical practice, with a small but significant proportion harboring malignancy. Conventional ultrasonography has limitations in differentiating benign from malignant nodules. Advanced imaging techniques such as spectral Doppler ultrasonography and diffusion-weighted magnetic resonance imaging (DW-MRI) with apparent diffusion coefficient (ADC) measurements may improve diagnostic accuracy. Aim The study aimed to assess the role of spectral Doppler ultrasound values of the superior thyroid artery in thyroid nodules and correlating with ADC values using diffusion-weighted imaging (DWI) to differentiate benign and malignant thyroid nodules. Materials and methods This cross-sectional study was conducted in the Department of Radiology, ACS Medical College and Hospital, Chennai, from November 2023 to November 2024. Forty-two patients aged 18-70 years with suspected thyroid nodules were included using purposive sampling. Spectral Doppler ultrasonography was performed to assess pulsatility index (PI) and resistive index (RI), followed by DW-MRI using a 1.5 Tesla Siemens Magnetom Essenza scanner for ADC value measurement. Histopathology served as the reference standard. Data were analyzed using SPSS version 26.0, with independent t-test and receiver operating characteristic (ROC) curve analysis; P < 0.05 was considered statistically significant. Results The majority of participants were females (71.4%) and belonged to the 41-50 years of age group (31.0%). Malignant nodules demonstrated significantly higher PI (1.30 vs. 0.87; P = 0.04) and RI (0.80 vs. 0.60; P = 0.02), along with significantly lower ADC values at b = 0 and b = 1000 s/mm2 (P < 0.05). ROC analysis showed excellent diagnostic performance with area under the curve values of 0.974 for ADC (b0), 0.984 for ADC (b1000), 0.993 for PI, and 0.978 for RI. Conclusion Spectral Doppler indices and ADC values are reliable noninvasive imaging biomarkers for differentiating benign from malignant thyroid nodules, with high diagnostic accuracy. Their combined use can enhance early diagnosis and reduce unnecessary invasive procedures.

title: Clinical Spectrum of Young-onset Hypertension: Diverse Etiologies, Target-organ Damage, and Diagnostic Challenges - A Seven-case Series.
abstract: Abstract Young-onset hypertension - defined as sustained blood pressure elevation presenting before the age of 40 years - is increasingly encountered in tertiary care settings in India. Unlike hypertension in older adults, it frequently harbors secondary etiologies, presents with severe target-organ damage, and poses considerable diagnostic challenges. This case series illustrates the clinical heterogeneity of the condition and highlights the importance of systematic evaluation in this population. We report seven cases (age range 19-38 years; six males, one female) presenting to a tertiary care teaching hospital. Secondary etiologies included biopsy-proven focal segmental glomerulosclerosis with nephrotic-range proteinuria (Case 1), bilateral ostial renal artery stenosis complicated by heart failure with reduced ejection fraction (Case 2), and hypertension associated with erythrocytosis under evaluation (Case 6). Hypertensive emergency with acute ischemic stroke and hemorrhagic transformation, complicated by hypertensive dilated cardiomyopathy, occurred in Case 7. Essential hypertension was established in Cases 3-5, with end-organ manifestations including hypomagnesemia-induced ventricular premature complexes (Case 4) and hypertensive retinopathy (Case 5). Diagnostic investigations included renal biopsy, renal Doppler ultrasonography, renal angiography, 24-h Holter monitoring, serum erythropoietin assay, and brain magnetic resonance imaging. Individualized antihypertensive regimens were supplemented by disease-specific interventions. Outcomes ranged from clinical stabilization to partial neurological recovery, reflecting the variable prognosis associated with delayed diagnosis and inadequate treatment. Young-onset hypertension is not a uniformly benign or essential condition. Systematic evaluation for secondary causes and comprehensive assessment of target-organ damage are critical, particularly in resource-limited settings where these steps are frequently deferred.

title: Chicken Bone-induced Esophageal Perforation in a Child Presenting with Extensive Cervico-Thoracic Prevertebral Abscess and Sepsis: A Rare Case Report.
abstract: Abstract Esophageal perforation following foreign body ingestion is an uncommon but potentially life-threatening condition in children, particularly when diagnosis is delayed. Sharp foreign bodies such as chicken bones may result in deep tissue injury, abscess formation, mediastinitis, and sepsis. We report the case of an 8-year-old boy who presented with throat pain, cough, vomiting, and epigastric pain following accidental ingestion of a chicken bone. Contrast-enhanced computed tomography and magnetic resonance imaging revealed an extensive cervico-thoracic prevertebral abscess extending from C2 to T6 with multiple air pockets and a retained foreign body at the T5-T6 level, suggestive of esophageal perforation. The patient underwent emergency right posterolateral thoracotomy with drainage of the abscess and removal of the impacted chicken bone. Intraoperative flexible esophagoscopy demonstrated a 1 cm perforation at the cricopharyngeal level. Definitive repair of the posterior esophageal rent was subsequently performed through a left cervical approach with reinforcement using a sternohyoid muscle flap. The postoperative course was complicated by anastomotic leak, high-output esophageal fistula, right vocal cord dysfunction, and Klebsiella pneumoniae sepsis. Conservative management with feeding gastrostomy and nutritional support resulted in gradual recovery, and follow-up contrast studies showed complete healing without residual leak or stricture formation. This case highlights the importance of maintaining a high index of suspicion in children with persistent symptoms following foreign body ingestion. Early imaging, prompt diagnosis, and multidisciplinary individualized management are essential to prevent severe complications and improve outcomes in pediatric esophageal perforation.

title: Predicting Outcomes in Spontaneous Intracerebral Hemorrhage Using Clinical and Computed Tomography Markers: A Prospective Study.
abstract: Background Spontaneous intracerebral hemorrhage (ICH) represents a disproportionately high stroke burden (20%-30%) in low- and middle-income countries like India, necessitating accurate, early risk stratification using readily available clinical and radiographic features. Materials and methods This prospective observational study included 185 patients with spontaneous ICH at a tertiary care center. Baseline clinical severity was assessed using the Glasgow Coma Scale (GCS) and the ICH score. Radiographic markers included hematoma volume, intraventricular hemorrhage (IVH), and radiographic signs (swirl, blend, black hole, satellite, and spot signs). The primary outcome was unfavorable functional status (modified Rankin scale: 4-6, including mortality) at 90 days. Univariate analyses focused on identifying predictors associated with a poor outcome, followed by multivariable logistic regression. Results The mean age was 56.0 ± 12.4 years, with 72.4% prevalence of hypertension. The unfavorable outcome rate was 37.3% (N = 69), with 22.2% mortality. Univariate analysis (P < 0.05) revealed strong associations between poor outcome and greater hematoma volume, lower GCS score, higher ICH score, IVH, swirl sign, blend sign, satellite sign, hydrocephalus, herniation, and ≥2 multiple noncontrast computed tomography (NCCT) signs. Multivariable analysis identified hematoma volume, GCS score, ICH score, herniation, satellite sign, and male gender as independent predictors. Conclusion Clinical severity indicators and multiple NCCT signs in univariate analysis serve as robust markers of poor functional outcome. The independent prognostic value of the satellite sign and herniation highlights the utility of readily available radiographic features for immediate risk stratification.

title: Predicting ISUP upgrading from biopsy to radical prostatectomy using an interpretable machine learning model with mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis: a retrospective study.
abstract: The International Society of Urological Pathology (ISUP) grade upgrading from biopsy to radical prostatectomy (RP) occurs in approximately 30%-40% of prostate cancer patients and may compromise treatment planning. Although multiparametric MRI (mpMRI) improves lesion characterization, prostatitis-like signal changes can mimic clinically significant cancer and confound radiological interpretation; however, no predictive model has incorporated mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis as a variable for ISUP upgrading. This single-center retrospective study enrolled 503 consecutive men who underwent "12+1"-core transperineal ultrasound-guided systematic biopsy supplemented by cognitive mpMRI-targeted cores followed by laparoscopic RP (from May 2021 to October 2024). Least absolute shrinkage and selection operator (LASSO) logistic regression with 10-fold cross-validation was used for feature selection, and six machine learning classifiers were trained and evaluated on an independent test set (7:3 split). ISUP upgrading occurred in 195 patients (38.8%), and mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis was significantly more prevalent in upgraded cases (27.2% vs 11.4%, P < 0.001). The random forest model achieved the highest weighted composite score (area under the receiver operating characteristic curve [ROC-AUC]: 0.823; average precision: 0.799) and was selected as the final model. SHapley Additive exPlanations (SHAP) analysis ranked feature importance as: basal tumor location (mean |SHAP|: 0.145), Prostate Imaging Reporting and Data System (PI-RADS) ≥4 (mean |SHAP|: 0.121), percentage of positive cores (mean |SHAP|: 0.100), maximum tumor diameter (mean |SHAP|: 0.062), and mpMRI-diagnosed prostatitis (mean |SHAP|: 0.040). title: Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging in locally advanced prostate cancer: the radiologist's perspective on staging, treatment planning, and response assessment.
abstract: Clinically locally advanced prostate cancer (PCa) is usually defined as cT3-T4 disease with or without regional nodal involvement. Multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI) is still the reference examination for local T staging because it combines high-resolution anatomic evaluation with functional information from diffusion-weighted imaging and, when performed, dynamic contrast-enhanced imaging. Its main strengths are the depiction of extraprostatic extension, seminal vesicle invasion, apical or bladder-neck involvement, and the delivery of side-specific information that surgeons and radiation oncologists need for planning. Its main limitation is reduced sensitivity for focal microscopic extension and for nodal metastases, for which prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA PET/CT) is more sensitive. In current practice, mpMRI and PSMA PET/CT therefore play complementary rather than competing roles: mpMRI defines the local extent of disease, whereas PSMA PET/CT refines nodal and distant staging. Beyond initial staging, mpMRI also contributes to surgical evaluation, radiotherapy target delineation, adaptive replanning after androgen deprivation therapy, and the detection of recurrence after treatment. Interpretation after hormonal therapy, surgery, or radiotherapy, however, requires awareness of treatment-related signal changes and of the risk of both under- and overcalling recurrence. This narrative review summarizes the radiologist's perspective on how mpMRI should be performed, interpreted, and reported in clinically locally advanced PCa. Particular emphasis is placed on staging, treatment planning, and response assessment within a multimodality imaging pathway.

title: Combined contrast-enhanced ultrasound and elastography for clinically significant prostate cancer detection after negative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging.
abstract: Background Diagnosing clinically significant prostate cancer (csPCa) is challenging in patients with negative multiparametric magnetic resonance imaging (mpMRI). This study aimed to assess the performance of contrast-enhanced ultrasound (CEUS) combined with real-time elastography (RTE) for csPCa detection in these patients. Methods A total of 243 patients with negative mpMRI who were scheduled for a biopsy were included in this study. CEUS and RTE were performed in all patients, and the images were rated on a five-point Likert scale. Patients with suspicious lesions (Likert ≥3) underwent a targeted biopsy (TB) in conjunction with a systematic biopsy (SB). Patients without suspicious lesions underwent SB alone. csPCa was primarily defined as a grade group of ≥2. Results The overall PCa detection rate was 19.8% (48/243), including 31 csPCa cases (12.8%) and 17 clinically insignificant PCa (insPCa) cases (7.0%). The combination of CEUS and RTE achieved significantly higher csPCa detection rates than the SB, CEUS, and RTE strategies (11.5 versus 5.3%, 8.2%, and 7.0%, respectively; all P < 0.05). Performing TB as an adjunct to SB in 99 patients with suspicious lesions led to additional diagnoses of csPCa in 18 patients at the expense of overdetecting insPCa in 2 patients. SB in 144 patients without suspicious lesions did not result in csPCa detection but resulted in overdetection of insPCa in 4 patients. Conclusions In patients with negative mpMRI, the combination of CEUS and RTE showed significant improvement in csPCa detection and application potential in reducing the need for a prostate biopsy in men without suspicious lesions.

title: Ultrasound localization microscopy reveals region-specific cerebrovascular responses to exercise in aged mice.
abstract: Abstract Aging is widely recognized to impair cerebrovascular structure and function, potentially compromising the vascular environment that supports hippocampal plasticity and adult neurogenesis. Whether exercise can reverse these age-related changes in vivo and what vascular mechanisms underlie such effects remain unclear. Ultrasound localization microscopy is one of the most powerful tools for addressing this question by enabling in vivo, super-resolution mapping of microvascular architecture and blood-flow dynamics across both cortical and deep brain regions. Therefore, this study used localization microscopy to reveal the region-specific cerebrovascular responses in aged mice after exercise. We used ultrasound localization microscopy to compare cerebrovascular structure and hemodynamics among young control mice, aged sedentary mice, and aged mice subjected to 4 weeks of treadmill exercise. We further integrated regional summary measurements and features using principal component analysis and an L2-regularized logistic-regression-based aging axis trained exclusively on young and aged sedentary controls, and found that exercise-trained aged mice shifted 74% toward the young vascular phenotype along the control-defined axis, driven primarily by hippocampal flow, radius, and velocity. Our findings show that 4 weeks of treadmill exercise partially shifted the aged cerebrovascular phenotype toward a younger state in a region-dependent manner, with the structural and hemodynamic responses occurring in the hippocampal and subcortical regions. This framework separates exercise-responsive from exercise-resistant components of cerebrovascular aging.

title: Outcome of Children Treated with Rituximab for Steroid-Resistant Nephrotic Syndrome: Renal Histopathology as a Response Marker.
abstract: Background Steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) in children remains a major therapeutic challenge. Although calcineurin inhibitors (CNIs) are commonly used as first-line therapy, a substantial proportion of patients fail to achieve remission, and prolonged use may result in nephrotoxicity. Rituximab has emerged as a potential therapeutic option for refractory SRNS; however, treatment responses appear variable, and the influence of underlying renal histopathology remains incompletely understood. Objectives To evaluate the association between renal histopathological findings and clinical response to rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS). Methods Study Design and Setting:This prospective observational study was conducted between 2011 and 2020 at a university-affiliated tertiary pediatric nephrology center. The study aimed to evaluate the efficacy of rituximab in children with calcineurin inhibitor-resistant steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome (SRNS) and to examine the association between renal histopathological findings and treatment response. Twenty-four children aged 2-12 years were enrolled.Follow-up:Patients were followed prospectively after completion of rituximab therapy through regular clinical and laboratory assessments. The mean follow-up duration after the last rituximab infusion was 5.1 years (range: 6 months-8 years).Treatment Response Definitions:Complete remission was defined according to International Pediatric Nephrology Association (IPNA) recommendations as a urine protein-to-creatinine ratio (UPCR) ≤20 mg/mmol (≤0.2 mg/mg) or negative/trace proteinuria on dipstick testing on at least three consecutive occasions.Partial remission was defined as a UPCR >20 mg/mmol but <200 mg/mmol together with serum albumin ≥30 g/L.No response was defined as failure to achieve either complete or partial remission.Genetic Evaluation:Genetic testing was performed in all patients with focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS), classic minimal change disease (MCD), and MCD with IgM deposition. No pathogenic or likely pathogenic variants associated with monogenic steroid-resistant nephrotic syndrome were identified in the tested patients. Genetic testing was not performed in patients with IgA nephropathy, membranous nephropathy, C1q nephropathy, or dense deposit disease. Results Twenty-four children with SRNS were included (13 males and 11 females; age range 2-12 years). Histopathological diagnoses included focal segmental glomerulosclerosis (FSGS) in 9 patients (37.5%), minimal change disease (MCD) in 4 (16.7%), MCD with IgM deposition in 6 (25.0%), dense deposit disease in 2 (8.3%), membranous nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), IgA nephropathy in 1 (4.2%), and C1q nephropathy in 1 (4.2%). Overall, 10 patients (41.7%) achieved complete remission and 3 (12.5%) achieved partial remission, predominantly among patients with MCD and MCD with IgM deposition. Responses were uncommon among patients with FSGS. Eleven patients (45.8%), all of whom were non-responders, progressed to end-stage kidney disease. No major adverse effects of rituximab were observed; mild infusion reactions occurred in three patients and mild cellulitis in one patient. Conclusion In this cohort of children with refractory SRNS, favorable responses to rituximab were observed predominantly among patients with CNI- resistant MCD and MCD with IgM deposition, whereas responses among patients with FSGS were uncommon. These findings suggest that renal histopathology may help identify patients more likely to benefit from rituximab therapy; however, the small sample size, heterogeneous histopathological distribution, and observational study design preclude definitive conclusions. Larger prospective multicenter studies incorporating comprehensive genetic evaluation are required to determine whether histopathology can serve as a reliable predictor of rituximab responsiveness.

title: Acute right ventricular response to transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement.
abstract: Background Changes in right ventricular (RV) function are frequent after transcatheter tricuspid valve replacement (TTVR), yet their mechanisms and prognostic implications remain incompletely defined. Aims We sought to characterise acute RV functional changes following TTVR and evaluate their prognostic impact. Methods This multicentre study included consecutive patients treated with TTVR between 2019 and 2025 with complete imaging data. RV function was assessed by echocardiography at baseline, intraprocedurally, and before discharge. RV end-systolic elastance (Ees), effective arterial elastance (Ea), and RV-pulmonary artery coupling (Ees/Ea) were derived from non-invasive single-beat pressure-volume loop analysis. Changes over time were assessed using paired tests, and associations with mortality were investigated using Cox regression analysis with Firth's penalised likelihood. Results Sixty-seven patients (median age 78 years; 72% female; EVOQUE n=49; LuX-Valve Plus n=18) were included. At discharge, both cohorts showed declines in absolute RV free-wall longitudinal strain (aRV-FWLS; -10.4%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -10.4%; p=0.001 for LuX-Valve Plus) and fractional area change (FAC; -18.0%; p<0.001 for EVOQUE; -13.5%; p=0.005 for LuX-Valve Plus). Overall, 58% of patients met the criteria for severe RV dysfunction after TTVR. Over a median follow-up of 19 months, 15 patients died. Device type, acute RV functional changes, Ees, and Ees/Ea were not associated with mortality (allp>0.05). In contrast, computed tomography-derived RV coupling (hazard ratio [HR] 0.02, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 0.01-0.89) and the coexistence of baseline longitudinal (tricuspid annular plane systolic excursion <17 mm and/or aRV-FWLS <23%) and circumferential (RV-FAC ≤35%) RV dysfunction (HR 3.93, 95% CI: 1.10-14.47) were associated with mortality. Conclusions TTVR is associated with an acute decline in RV systolic function. Although common, early postprocedural RV dysfunction was not associated with midterm mortality.

title: Prediction of coronary events by computed tomography-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio.
abstract: Background Coronary computed tomography angiography (CCTA)-derived Murray law-based quantitative flow ratio (CT-μFR) provides a non-invasive measure of vessel-level ischaemia but may not capture local haemodynamic abnormalities reflected by the longitudinal pressure gradient across the lesion (CT-μFR gradient). Aims We aimed to evaluate the association of CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient with 3-year vessel-level subsequent coronary events and to determine the incremental prognostic value of their combined assessment. Methods Our study included a total of 885 vessels from 312 patients who underwent invasive coronary angiography for acute coronary syndrome (ACS) or stable angina and had prior CCTA performed 6 months to 3 years earlier. CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient were assessed by an independent core laboratory blinded to the clinical data. The primary outcome was 3-year subsequent coronary events (a composite of vessel-specific myocardial infarction or urgent revascularisation for ACS). The discrimination ability of predictive models was assessed using Harrell's C-index. Results Vessels with CT-μFR ≤0.80 or a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm had a higher risk of events than those with CT-μFR>0.80 (79.1% vs 20.4%, adjusted hazard ratio [HR] 6.87, 95% confidence interval [CI]: 5.26-8.96; p<0.001) or a CT-μFR gradient <0.004/mm (72.6% vs 27.4%, adjusted HR 4.08, 95% CI: 3.15-5.28; p<0.001), respectively. Among vessels with CT-μFR>0.80, a CT-μFR gradient ≥0.004/mm remained associated with increased risk (adjusted HR 2.59, 95% CI: 1.63-4.11; p<0.001). Adding the CT-μFR gradient to CT-μFR improved discrimination in the overall cohort (C-index 0.700 to 0.755; p<0.001) as well as the subgroup with CT-μFR>0.80 (C-index 0.575 to 0.655; p<0.001). Conclusions Both CT-μFR and the CT-μFR gradient are independently associated with 3-year subsequent coronary events. Their combined assessment improves risk stratification beyond CT-μFR alone. (ClinicalTrials.gov: NCT04794868).

title: Virtual non-calcium dual-energy computed tomography for postoperative lumbar spine evaluation following pedicle screw instrumentation.
abstract: Purpose To compare standard grayscale CT, 140-keV virtual monoenergetic imaging, and virtual non-calcium (VNCa) for detection of magnetic resonance imaging (MRI)-defined relevant foraminal stenosis, disc protrusion or extrusion, and relevant nerve root compression. Methods This retrospective study included patients who underwent dual-energy computed tomography (DECT) on a 128-slice single-tube system and MRI within 1 week between August and December 2025; CT reconstructions were read in consensus. Foraminal stenosis and nerve root compression grades 2-3 were considered imaging-defined relevant findings. Only segments with an MRI confidence score of 5 were included. Diagnostic performance and CT confidence scores were summarized descriptively. Results Twenty-three patients (mean age, 60 ± 12 years; 15 women) contributed 185 evaluated segments. MRI showed relevant foraminal stenosis in 26 segments and disc protrusion or extrusion and relevant nerve root compression in 18 segments each. Foraminal-stenosis sensitivity was 100.0% (26/26) for VNCa and 92.3% (24/26) for both comparators; specificity was 88.7%, 71.1%, and 72.3% for VNCa, standard CT, and 140-keV CT, respectively. Disc protrusion or extrusion sensitivity was 77.8% (14/18) for VNCa and 11.1% (2/18) for both comparators. Standard CT and VNCa each had 83.3% sensitivity and 97.0% specificity for nerve root compression. Conclusion In this small, selected cohort, VNCa had higher observed specificity for MRI-defined foraminal stenosis and higher observed sensitivity for disc protrusion or extrusion. These exploratory findings require confirmation in larger studies that account for patient-level clustering and include more artifact-limited examinations. Clinical significance VNCa reconstruction from an existing DECT examination may complement grayscale CT for evaluating MRI-defined foraminal stenosis and disc protrusion or extrusion following lumbar pedicle screw instrumentation without requiring additional scanning.

title: Large language models in radiology: a bibliometric analysis of growth, collaboration, and thematic shifts (November 2022-July 2026).
abstract: Purpose To map the development of research on large language models (LLMs) in radiology from November 2022 to July 2026, focusing on publication trends, collaboration patterns, citation distribution, and thematic shifts among Science Citation Index Expanded (SCIE)-indexed original research articles. Methods A bibliometric analysis was conducted using records retrieved from the Web of Science Core Collection. Terms related to LLMs and radiology were combined at the topic (title, abstract, and keyword) level, and records retrieved by a complementary title-restricted strategy were screened jointly so that the analytic corpus reflected the union of both strategies. Only original research articles indexed in the SCIE were included. Records were screened independently by three reviewers (Fleiss' κ: 0.67). Publication trends, leading countries, institutions, authors, and journals; international collaboration networks; keyword co-occurrence patterns; citation distributions; and period-stratified thematic shifts were analyzed. Citation concentration was assessed with year-stratified sensitivity analyses, and a post hoc vision-language and foundation model sensitivity search quantified recent literature not captured by the primary strategy. Results A total of 850 SCIE-indexed articles were included. Annual output increased from 1 article in 2022 to 380 in 2025 (2026 partial). The dataset accumulated 10,767 citations (mean 12.67 per article; Hirsch index 48), but impact was concentrated: The 10% most cited articles accounted for 63.8% of all citations, and 28.5% of articles were uncited (8.0% excluding the partial 2026 window). The United States was the most productive country and the most connected hub of international collaboration by total link strength and betweenness centrality, followed by China, Germany, and Türkiye. Publications concentrated in a small number of high-impact journals, led by Radiology . Keyword and period-stratified analyses showed a shift from early ChatGPT-centered feasibility studies toward general LLM and modality-specific evaluation, with keyword-level signals of an emerging multimodal direction. Conclusion Research on LLMs in the SCIE-indexed radiology literature has expanded rapidly since 2022. Keyword patterns suggest a gradual shift from exploratory, text-only applications toward clinically oriented evaluation, with early keyword-level signals of a multimodal direction, although methodological heterogeneity and the absence of standardized, clinically meaningful evaluation frameworks remain the main barriers to clinical adoption. Clinical significance By quantifying where, by whom, and on which themes LLM research in radiology is produced, this analysis helps radiologists, researchers, and funders identify under-studied modalities and applications, locate established collaboration networks, and direct future work toward the standardized, clinically meaningful evaluation frameworks the field currently lacks.

title: Magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction and selected quantitative ultrasound methods for hepatic steatosis: histology-referenced diagnostic performance and longitudinal responsiveness-a systematic review and meta-analysis.
abstract: Purpose To synthesize histology-referenced diagnostic performance at study-selected thresholds and the longitudinal responsiveness of magnetic resonance imaging proton density fat fraction (MRI-PDFF) and selected quantitative ultrasound methods in adults with non-alcoholic fatty liver disease/metabolic dysfunction-associated steatotic liver disease. Methods Four databases were searched from database inception through July 1, 2026. Sensitivity, specificity, and odds ratios were pooled with 95% confidence intervals using heterogeneity-selected fixed- or random-effects models. Small-study effects were assessed using funnel plots and Begg tests; longitudinal changes were pooled when change-score standard deviations were reported. Results In total, 44 articles were included: 34 contributed histology-referenced diagnostic data, and 11 were assessed for longitudinal responsiveness, with 1 article contributing to both. At steatosis grade (S) ≥ 1/S ≥ 2/S ≥3, MRI-PDFF sensitivity and specificity was 93.6%/81.5%/83.1% and 87.1%/86.7%/83.2%, respectively; the controlled attenuation parameter (CAP) was 86.8%/81.2%/86.4% and 98.9%/71.0%/64.6%, respectively. The attenuation coefficient/attenuation imaging sensitivity/specificity was 83.2%/98.1%, 86.4%/79.9%, and 99.3%/76.4%, respectively. Ultrasound-guided attenuation parameter and ultrasound-derived fat fraction evidence was limited. Three head-to-head longitudinal studies included 298 participants, of whom only 158 had analyzable change-score data; in these, pooled changes were -4.53 percentage points for MRI-PDFF and -12.71 dB/m for the CAP. Thirty-two of the 34 diagnostic studies were at high-risk of bias from cohort-selected thresholds. Begg tests did not detect significant small-study effects, although their power was very limited in analyses that included only 2 or 3 studies. Conclusion At study-selected thresholds, MRI-PDFF showed balanced sensitivity and specificity across steatosis grades, whereas quantitative ultrasound varied by method, platform, and threshold. These findings support comparative synthesis but do not establish validated cut-offs or superiority of either modality. Clinical significance Study-selected thresholds limit clinical translation. MRI-PDFF proton density fat fraction and quantitative ultrasound are complementary, with use depending on clinical purpose, platform, and precision needs.

title: Comparative reasoning in radiology artificial intelligence: longitudinal and reference-case approaches.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) in radiology remains predominantly examination-centric, whereas clinical interpretation frequently depends on comparison across time or with relevant prior cases. This narrative review examines comparative reasoning in radiology AI through two related but clinically distinct forms: longitudinal reasoning, which compares examinations from the same patient over time, and reference-case reasoning, which uses clinically analogous cases from other patients to support interpretation. We propose a capability hierarchy that distinguishes simple access to comparative information from higher-level capabilities, including selection of relevant historical context, anatomical and lesion-level correspondence, characterization of interval change, temporal-state interpretation, multi-interval trajectory reasoning, and entity-specific assessment of clinical similarity. This distinction matters because providing prior examinations or retrieving visually similar cases does not itself demonstrate meaningful comparative reasoning. We review developments in prior-examination selection, registration, lesion tracking, temporal vision-language modeling, treatment-response assessment, analogous-case retrieval, and longitudinal report generation. Particular emphasis is placed on evaluation strategies that determine whether model performance depends appropriately on clinically relevant comparative information rather than on additional input volume, global image similarity, acquisition characteristics, or other shortcuts. Key challenges include incorrect prior selection, lesion mismatching, temporal inconsistency, clinically irrelevant reference-case retrieval, data leakage, misleading comparative language, and propagation of historical errors. Future progress will require models that preserve entity identity, reason coherently across multi-visit imaging histories, identify clinically informative reference cases, and demonstrate benefit under realistic clinical conditions. Comparative reasoning is therefore a necessary step in the transition from examination-level toward patient-level radiology AI.

title: Additive Value of Whole-body CT in Patients Imaged with PET/CT for Solitary Pulmonary Nodules.
abstract: Objectives In routine positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) imaging of solitary pulmonary nodules (SPNs), CT acquisition is typically performed from the vertex to the mid-thigh. The administered 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose ( 18 F-FDG) dose is adjusted according to patient weight and is independent of the scanned body region; however, radiation exposure from the CT component increases with scan length. In this study, we aimed to evaluate the clinical value of extrathoracic CT imaging in patients undergoing PET/CT for SPN characterization and to quantify the potential reduction in radiation dose when CT is limited to the thorax. Methods A total of 154 patients who underwent 18 F-FDG PET/CT for the evaluation of SPNs between 2009 and 2011 were retrospectively analyzed. None of the patients had a prior diagnosis of malignancy or had received chemotherapy or radiotherapy. Incidental extrathoracic CT findings were classified as major, moderate, or minor according to their clinical significance. CT radiation dose was estimated using dose-length product (DLP) values. PET findings, incidental CT findings, radiation dose, and acquisition times were evaluated. Results Extrathoracic CT findings were detected in 61 patients (39%), with a total of 86 incidental lesions. However, only 3 patients (2%) had major extrathoracic findings requiring urgent clinical intervention. Two of these were osteolytic bone lesions that were 18 F-FDG avid and potantially detectable on whole-body PET. Extrathoracic 18 F-FDG uptake was observed in 10 patients (6.5%). The mean DLP was 458.3±70.5 mGy cm for whole-body CT and 130.8±9.1 mGy cm for thorax-only CT, corresponding to a 3.5-fold higher CT radiation dose (p<0.01). A PET-based protocol, however, prolongs acquisition time by approximately 6 minutes. Conclusion In SPN PET/CT evaluation, routine body CT does does not provide clinically significant additional information in most patients but substantially increases radiation exposure. Performing thoracic CT following whole-body PET, with additional targeted CT only when extrathoracic PET abnormalities are detected, may reduce radiation exposure while preserving the diagnostic information provided by CT of the thorax. However, such an approach prolongs acquisition time and increases workload.

title: Comparison of Classical Image Processing Methods and the Artificial Intelligence-Based MedSAM2 Model for Liver Tumor Segmentation in Radioembolization Dosimetry: A LiTS Dataset Analysis.
abstract: Objectives Accurate estimation of tumor and critical organ doses in radioembolization therapy is essential for treatment planning. The choice of segmentation technique used in voxel-based dosimetry can affect the calculated volumes and dose estimates. In this study, the liver tumor segmentation performances of classical image processing methods and a pretrained artificial intelligence (AI) Medical Segment Anything Model 2 (MedSAM2) were compared, along with their effects on a simplified dose-change indicator. title: Interval Progression Before <sup>177</sup>Lu-PSMA Mimicking Treatment Failure on Interim PSMA PET/CT.
abstract: Interpretation of follow-up prostate-specific membrane antigen positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PSMA PET/CT) during lutetium-177-labeled PSMA ( 177 Lu-PSMA) radioligand therapy (RLT) may be misleading if rapid disease progression occurs between baseline PSMA PET/CT and initiation of RLT. A 78-year-old man with metastatic castration-resistant prostate cancer underwent baseline gallium-68-PSMA PET/CT to assess eligibility for 177 Lu-PSMA-RLT and was deemed eligible. Interim PSMA PET/CT after 2 cycles showed multiple new lesions and an increased total tumor burden, suggesting progressive disease. However, these lesions were already visible on post-therapy single-photon emission computed tomography (SPECT)/CT after cycle 1, indicating interval progression between baseline PSMA PET/CT and initiation of 177 Lu-PSMA-RLT rather than treatment failure. In rapidly progressive disease, cycle-1 post-therapy SPECT/CT may provide a true imaging baseline for response assessment.

title: The Prognostic Value of <sup>18</sup>F-FDG PET/CT Parameters in Mantle Cell Lymphoma: A Retrospective Single-Center Study.
abstract: Objectives Mantle cell lymphoma (MCL) is an aggressive subtype of non-Hodgkin lymphoma for which accurate early prognostication is crucial. This study primarily investigated the potential of quantitative metabolic parameters derived from baseline and interim 18 F-fluorodeoxyglucose positron emission tomography/computed tomography (PET/CT) scans to independently predict treatment response and survival outcomes in patients with MCL. Methods A total of 48 newly diagnosed MCL patients were retrospectively enrolled in a cohort; of these, 32 patients had interim PET/CT scans analyzed. Semi-quantitative parameters, including standardized uptake value (SUV) and its normalizations, alongside quantitative volumetric parameters such as total body metabolic tumor volume (tMTV) and total body total lesion glycolysis (tTLG), were measured. Independent prognostic factors were determined by Cox regression analysis. Results A strong reduction in SUV, tTLG, and tMTV values between baseline and interim PET/CT verified a significant metabolic response to treatment. Interim volumetric parameters, specifically tTLG and tMTV, demonstrated superior performance in predicting treatment response. Multivariate Cox regression analysis identified tMTV and SUV normalized to body surface area (SUV bsa ) as independent prognostic factors for progression-free survival (PFS). Kaplan-Meier analysis revealed that high baseline SUV bsa and high interim SUV values were strongly associated with poor survival outcomes. Overall survival was not independently associated with any PET/CT parameter in the multivariate model. Conclusion In MCL patients, baseline SUV bsa and quantitative parameters derived from interim PET/CT are powerful and independent biomarkers for PFS. These data can improve prognostic stratification and guide risk-adapted therapies by enabling the early identification of high-risk patients.

title: A Simple Preoperative Computed Tomography Difficulty Score for Planned Video-assisted Thoracoscopic Lobectomy: A Retrospective Exploratory Study.
abstract: Objective Technical difficulty during video-assisted thoracoscopic surgery (VATS) lobectomy may not be fully captured by conversion to thoracotomy. We evaluated whether a simple preoperative computed tomography (CT) difficulty score could identify patients at increased risk of difficult VATS lobectomy. Material and methods This single-center retrospective study included patients who underwent planned standard VATS lobectomy with complete CT score data. The author-developed exploratory 0-3 score assigned one point each to the hilar, pleuroparenchymal inflammatory, and obstructive/emphysematous domains. The primary composite endpoint was defined as unplanned conversion to thoracotomy, major intraoperative bleeding, or an operative duration of at least 360 minutes. The duration criterion applied only to completed VATS procedures. The major technical endpoint of the secondary objective was conversion or major bleeding. Scores of 0-1 and 2-3 were defined as low and high CT burden, respectively. Results Fifty patients were analyzed; 42 completed VATS and 8 underwent conversion. Major bleeding occurred in two patients, and 11 of 42 completed VATS procedures met the prolonged-duration criterion. The primary and secondary endpoints occurred in 19 (38.0%) and 9 (18.0%) patients, respectively. A high CT burden was present in 12 patients and was associated with higher rates of the primary endpoint (66.7% vs. 28.9%; P = 0.038) and of the secondary endpoint (41.7% vs. 10.5%; P = 0.027). High CT burden was associated with the primary endpoint [odds ratios (ORs) 4.91, 95% confidence interval (CI) 1.22-19.71] and the secondary endpoint (OR 6.07, 95% CI 1.29-28.49). The corresponding area under the curve were 0.634 and 0.672. Conclusion In this retrospective cohort, a CT difficulty score ≥2 was associated with higher observed rates of difficult VATS and objective major technical events. Discrimination was modest, and confidence intervals were wide; the score is hypothesis-generating rather than validated, and it requires standardized CT reassessment and external validation.

title: Diagnostic performance of ChatGPT in adnexal mass classification: A comparative study with frozen section and final histopathology.
abstract: Objective To evaluate the diagnostic performance of ChatGPT in classifying adnexal masses as benign, borderline, or malignant, and to compare its performance with intraoperative frozen-section analysis, using final histopathology as the reference standard. Materials and methods This retrospective, observational, comparative study included 259 patients who underwent surgery for ovarian masses between January 2021 and July 2025. Preoperative clinical data, laboratory parameters, and ultrasonographic findings were recorded. ChatGPT assessments were performed using structured clinical inputs without prompt optimization. Frozen section diagnoses and ChatGPT classifications were compared with final histopathological results. Diagnostic performance metrics, including sensitivity, specificity, positive predictive value (PPV), negative predictive value (NPV), Cohen's kappa coefficient, and area under the curve (AUC), were calculated. Results According to final histopathology, 83.4% of cases were benign, 7.7% were borderline, and 8.9% were malignant. Frozen section analysis demonstrated high diagnostic accuracy, with sensitivity and specificity of 94.4% and 100%, respectively, when borderline cases were excluded. In comparison, ChatGPT showed a sensitivity of 90.0% and a specificity of 92.5%. The PPV for ChatGPT (56.3%) was markedly lower than that for frozen section (100%), whereas NPV values were comparable (98.9% vs. 99.5%). When borderline tumors were classified as malignant, ChatGPT's performance declined further, with a sensitivity of 74.4%, a specificity of 79.6%, and a PPV of 42.1%. Receiver operating characteristic analysis showed AUCs of 0.967 for the frozen section and 0.893 for ChatGPT. ChatGPT demonstrated a higher rate of false-positive classifications, particularly in the borderline and malignant categories. Conclusion Frozen section analysis remains a highly reliable method for intraoperative evaluation of ovarian tumors. Although ChatGPT demonstrates good discriminative ability and high NPV, its lower specificity and PPV limit its role as a standalone diagnostic tool. ChatGPT may serve as a complementary decision-support tool, particularly in ruling out malignancy, but cannot replace histopathological evaluation.

title: Anatomy- and venous dominance-guided outflow reconstruction for left-sided pediatric liver grafts: algorithm, technique, and donor pool expansion.
abstract: Background Variant left hepatic vein (LHV) and middle hepatic vein (MHV) anatomy complicates venous outflow reconstruction in pediatric living donor liver transplantation (LDLT). We evaluated an anatomy- and venous dominance-guided reconstruction strategy for left-sided grafts. Methods We retrospectively studied 77 consecutive pediatric LDLTs using left-sided grafts (2017-2025). Donor venous anatomy was assessed with three-dimensional computed tomography, and reconstruction was performed using a predefined anatomy- and dominance-based algorithm. Results Of the 77 recipients, 57 (74.0%) received left lateral segment (LLS) grafts and 20 (26.0%) received left lobe (LL) grafts. In the LLS cohort, LHV anatomy was classified as type 1 in 33 donors (57.9%), a type 1 variant in 1 (1.8%), type 2 in 13 (22.8%), and type 3 in 10 (17.5%). Type 1 required no reconstruction, type 2 underwent venoplasty, and type 3 required tailored reconstruction based on dominance; right hepatic vein-dominant grafts (n=6) underwent selective MHV inclusion to obtain a single, anatomically aligned unified outflow, whereas MHV-dominant grafts (n=4) required bench neo-LHV reconstruction. Among LL grafts, 12 donors (60.0%) had standard grafts with complete MHV inclusion, while 8 (40.0%) required modified procurement (subtotal, partial, or no MHV inclusion). Hepatic venous outflow obstruction (HVOO) occurred in three patients (3.9%); two LLS recipients (MHV-dominant type 3) required endovascular intervention, while one modified LL recipient was managed conservatively. No donor complications were observed. Conclusions Anatomy- and venous dominance-guided reconstruction safely expands the use of left-sided grafts, minimizes unnecessary reconstruction, maintains low HVOO rates, and broadens the pediatric living donor pool.

title: Implementing Standardized Screening and Detection of Cognitive Impairment and Brain Pathologies in People with Spinal Cord Injury or Disease During First Rehabilitation: A Prospective Observational Study.
abstract: Objectives This study aims to evaluate the effectiveness of implementing a hospital-specific standard for screening for cognitive impairments and structural brain pathologies, as well as their prevalence during first rehabilitation in people with traumatic or nontraumatic spinal cord injury or disease (SCI/D). Method This was a prospective observational study in a specialized clinic using a hospital-specific assessment standard during first rehabilitation after SCI/D including the Montreal Cognitive Assessment (MoCA) and structural brain magnetic resonance imaging (MRI) about 3 months after the onset of SCI/D. Individuals aged ≥18, with acute traumatic/nontraumatic SCI/D, admitted after July 15, 2019, and discharged before June 30, 2022, were consecutively included. Logistic regression examined associations between screening completion, pathologies, and clinical characteristics. Results Of 215 participants (median age 58 [IQR 38-70]; 74% male; 66% traumatic SCI), 73% ( n = 156) underwent brain MRI and 70% ( n = 151) completed the MoCA. MRI revealed pathologies in 59.8% ( n = 64) of traumatic SCI and 70.8% ( n = 34) of SCD patients. MoCA scores were 18 to 25 in 29 patients and 10 to 17 in 7; one patient had a score <10. Seven individuals showed cognitive impairment (6 mild, 1 severe) despite unremarkable brain scans. Older age (≥65) (42%; n = 23) was associated with lower MoCA scores. Demographical bias did not significantly influence screening completion. Conclusion Implementing a hospital-specific standard increased screening rates regardless of age, trauma, or lesion level. Individuals with traumatic SCI and older adults with SCD were high-risk groups. The mismatch between MRI and MoCA findings highlights the necessity of a multimodal diagnostic approach.

title: Prehabilitation of loss-of-domain ventral hernias: Integrating botulinum toxin A, progressive pneumoperitoneum, and CT volumetry.
abstract: Loss of domain ventral and incisional hernias are an anatomic and physiologic challenge because chronic visceral externalization, lateral muscle retraction, and limited abdominal capacity can make reduction and primary fascial closure hazardous. This review searched PubMed/MEDLINE through 20 August 2026 and used backward and forward citation tracking to examine computed tomography (CT) volumetry, botulinum toxin type A (BTA), and progressive preoperative pneumoperitoneum (PPP). The Tanaka ratio [hernia sac volume (HSV)/abdominal cavity volume (ACV)] and Sabbagh ratio [HSV/(HSV+ACV)] must be reported by name because their percentages are not interchangeable: A Tanaka ratio of 25% corresponds to a Sabbagh ratio of 20% for the same volumes. BTA consistently elongates the lateral abdominal wall, but comparative evidence for improved clinical outcomes is mixed and remains non-randomized. PPP expands abdominal capacity; however, direct respiratory evidence is limited and conflicting, and procedure-related complications are relevant. A multicenter comparison found no additional volumetric benefit from adding BTA to PPP, while a 2025 propensity-matched meta-analysis found no significant improvement in closure, recurrence, component separation, or wound outcomes with BTA. The large 2026 Hospital La Fe series used combined BTA and PPP in all 220 patients; its proposed threshold-based pathway therefore should not be interpreted as a validated comparison of BTA alone versus combined therapy. We propose a cautious, evidence-informed framework in which CT phenotype, named volumetric formula, reducibility, respiratory reserve, and reconstructive requirements are considered together. The framework is hypothesis-generating rather than a validated treatment algorithm.

title: Treatment-Response Evidence, Care-Pathway Gaps, and Guideline Discordance in Gastric MALT Lymphoma: An Umbrella Review.
abstract: Background/aims Reviews of gastric mucosa-associated lymphoid tissue lymphoma have quantified treatment response, but their coverage of the care pathway and relationship to guideline differences remain unclear. Methods PubMed, Embase, and the Cochrane Library were searched through March 31, 2026. Eligible reviews were mapped to 13 clinical questions as direct, partial, or absent coverage. Question-specific anchors were selected without pooling overlapping reviews. All 16 items of A MeaSurement Tool to Assess systematic Reviews, version 2 were examined; overall confidence was assigned to intervention reviews. European Gastro-Intestinal Lymphoma Study, European Society for Medical Oncology, National Comprehensive Cancer Network, and British Society for Haematology recommendations were compared descriptively. Results Fifteen reviews were eligible; nine reviews answered seven questions. Complete remission was 75.2% after successful Helicobacter pylori eradication in H. pylori -positive disease. In H. pylori -negative disease, source-defined complete remission was 29.3%, including probable minimal residual disease. Remission was 22.2% in patients with t(11;18)/ BIRC3::MALT1 -positive disease versus 78.0% in patients with translocation-negative disease. The radiotherapy remission estimates were 97.3% after eradication failure and 96.0% in the limited-stage cohort. Gastric positron emission tomography (PET) detection was 62.0%, without evidence of management benefit. All eight intervention reviews had critically low confidence; seven nonintervention reviews received descriptive profiles. The guidelines differed for H. pylori -negative management, endoscopic ultrasonography, bone marrow biopsy, and PET/computed tomography. No eligible review compared the relevant treatment sequences or staging strategies. Conclusions Review-level evidence is concentrated on treatment response. It cannot establish superiority between treatment sequences or determine staging, escalation timing, surveillance, or relapse strategies. Guideline differences concern decisions for which the relevant comparisons remain unsynthesized.

title: Preliminary Experience with Simultaneous Bilateral Radiofrequency Vim Thalamotomy: Two Cases Including the First Participant in a Prospective Trial.
abstract: Background Simultaneous bilateral thalamotomy has historically been discouraged because of neurological risks. Case report We report a retrospective index case and the first participant in an ongoing prospective trial undergoing simultaneous bilateral radiofrequency Vim thalamotomy. A stepwise intraoperative MRI protocol was used in the prospective case. At 6 months, CRST improved by 91.2% and 70.2%, respectively. Transient dysarthria and dysphagia resolved, no gait or balance disturbance was observed, and mild lingual paresthesia persisted in Case 2. Discussion These preliminary findings support continued prospective evaluation of a lesion-minimizing strategy.

title: Non-nutritional rickets: Approach, precision medicine, and outcomes.
abstract: Rickets are chronic bone disorders marked by impaired mineralization of the growing skeleton. While most cases arise from nutritional deficiencies, non-nutritional forms are frequently underrecognized. Subtle signs such as alopecia in vitamin D dependent rickets type 2A, cataract in Lowe syndrome, dental abscesses or sensorineural hearing loss in X-linked hypophosphatemia can prompt timely diagnosis and referral. A structured approach combining growth and skeletal assessment, targeted biochemistry (calcium, phosphate, alkaline phosphatase, parathyroid hormone, 25-hydroxyvitamin D, 1,25-dihydroxyvitamin D), radiography, and early genetic testing once nutritional deficiency or renal failure are excluded improves diagnostic accuracy. Molecular confirmation enables precise subclassification into hypophosphatemic and calciopenic rickets, supporting genotype-directed therapy, including burosumab for X-linked hypophosphatemia. Early, tailored treatment enhances radiographic healing, growth, and function. Emerging genotype-phenotype correlations further inform genetic counselling and prognosis, strengthening the multidisciplinary management of these complex disorders.

title: A Primer on Radiomics for the Practicing Orthopaedic Surgeon.
abstract: Artificial intelligence (AI) is permeating many aspects of daily life. Medicine, and specifically orthopaedic surgery, is being influenced by the rapid growth and success of AI in serving as an adjunct to medical expertise. AI includes many nested subfields and applications such as computer vision, language models, and predictive analytics. Using standard machine learning methods, clinical decision support tools are being developed for clinicians to provide evidence-based, individualized care. Some models predict clinical and functional outcomes after a procedure, whereas others may incorporate administrative metrics to predict factors, such as length of stay, return to the emergency department, and complications. The application of AI to medical imaging focuses on the extraction of a large amount of quantitative data in the form of predefined features from clinical images that humans cannot perceive, a field known as radiomics. There has been recent interest, particularly in oncology, to apply radiomics to aid in diagnosis and prognostication of outcomes. Given the robust growth of radiomics literature, and the anticipated application in orthopaedic surgery, the purpose of this review article is to educate the orthopaedic surgery community on the practical importance and the basics of radiomics.

title: Cardiac Magnetic Resonance in MINOCA: From Diagnosis to Phenotyping.
abstract: Myocardial infarction with non-obstructive coronary arteries (MINOCA) is a working diagnosis established after coronary angiography and requires further evaluation to distinguish true ischemic MINOCA from alternative non-ischemic diagnoses. Accurate identification of the underlying etiology is essential because prognosis and management vary substantially among disease entities. Cardiac magnetic resonance (CMR) has emerged as the central noninvasive imaging modality in the diagnostic evaluation of MINOCA. This review summarizes the role of CMR in patients presenting with MINOCA, focusing on diagnostic pathways, tissue characterization techniques, phenotypic classification, prognostic assessment, clinical practice, and emerging technologies. CMR enables comprehensive assessment of ventricular function, myocardial edema, fibrosis, necrosis, and microvascular injury through cine imaging, T1- and T2-based tissue characterization, and late gadolinium enhancement. By integrating these findings, CMR differentiates patients with true ischemic MINOCA from those with alternative non-ischemic diagnoses, thereby guiding subsequent investigations and management. Early CMR substantially increases diagnostic yield and frequently identifies a specific etiology that directly influences treatment decisions. Beyond diagnosis, CMR provides important prognostic information through the quantification of infarct size, microvascular obstruction, myocardial edema, and scar burden. Advanced parametric mapping techniques and artificial intelligence-assisted image analysis may further refine disease phenotyping and improve risk stratification.

title: Unintended coverage: how standard breast radiotherapy irradiates the internal mammary nodes.
abstract: Background Breast cancer is the most common malignancy in women worldwide. Irradiation of regional nodes, including the internal mammary nodes (IMNs), may improve outcomes, but routine IMN irradiation remains controversial because of toxicity. Modern breast radiotherapy may incidentally irradiate the ipsilateral IMNs. We quantified incidental IMN doses and factors affecting coverage in patients without targeted IMN irradiation. Materials and methods In this retrospective dosimetric study, 104 women with clinical stage I-III disease were analysed. The ipsilateral IMNs (levels I-III) were contoured on planning CT scans according to the RTOG guidelines. Dose-volume histogram (DVH) metrics (minimum, mean, and maximum doses; V 95% , V 90% , and V 50% ) were recorded. Group comparisons [mastectomy vs . breast-conserving surgery (BCS) and 3DCRT vs . VMAT)] were performed using statistical tests, with p < 0.05 considered statistically significant. Results The median age was 52 years; 56.7% of patients were aged > 50 years; left- and right-sided tumours were equally represented. Seventy-five per cent underwent mastectomy and 25% underwent BCS. Eighty-one per cent received 3DCRT; 46% received supraclavicular/axillary irradiation; the median follow-up was 40 months. The mean IMN volume was 7.30 ± 1.76 cm 3 . The mean IMN dose was 35.53 ± 6.20 Gy, and the minimum dose was 7.73 ± 6.37 Gy. On average, 47.3% of the IMN volume received ≥ 95% of the prescribed dose. Mastectomy plans delivered a higher mean IMN dose than BCS plans (36.55 vs . 32.48 Gy, p = 0.0046). 3DCRT plans provided better IMN coverage than VMAT plans (mean V 95% , 51.4% vs . 29.1%; p = 0.0012). Radiotherapy modality and type of surgery were significant in the multivariate analysis. Conclusions Standard tangential fields provide only partial IMN coverage with wide variability. Most patients did not reach therapeutic IMN doses, highlighting the need for explicit contouring and dedicated planning when IMN irradiation is indicated.
