title: Guided bone regeneration with polytetrafluoroethylene titanium-reinforced membrane, CAD/CAM semi-occlusive titanium mesh and CAD/CAM occlusive titanium foil in partially atrophic arches: A comparative randomised controlled trial with 3-year follow-up.
abstract: Purpose To evaluate the effectiveness of three distinct guided bone regeneration devices, namely non-resorbable polytetrafluoroethylene membrane, semi-occlusive CAD/CAM titanium mesh and occlusive CAD/CAM titanium foil, over a 3-year period, focusing on clinical and radiographic outcomes. Materials and methods Twenty-seven partially edentulous patients with alveolar atrophy requiring guided bone regeneration for implant placement were enrolled and randomly allocated to one of three treatment groups (polytetrafluoroethylene, mesh or foil). Surgical time and surgical satisfaction were assessed and compared among the groups. The present study reports the 3-year clinical outcomes update, including marginal bone loss and complications. Results Mean marginal bone loss at 3 years was 0.82 ± 0.46 mm in the polytetrafluoroethylene group, 0.95 ± 0.36 mm in the mesh group and 0.92 ± 0.61 mm in the foil group, with no significant association between device type. Six bone augmentation-related complications occurred, with no significant difference among groups (P = 0.842). Five implant-related complications were recorded among 60 implants (P = 0.730), including one implant failure; no prosthetic failures occurred. Smoking was significantly associated with greater marginal bone loss at 3 years (P = 0.015). CAD/CAM mesh and foil were associated with shorter surgical times and greater surgeon satisfaction than polytetrafluoroethylene membrane. Conclusions All three guided bone regeneration devices were associated with favourable and comparable clinical and radiographic outcomes at 3 years. Customised CAD/CAM titanium mesh and foil maintained good peri-implant bone stability similar to titanium-reinforced polytetrafluoroethylene membrane, while offering advantages in intraoperative handling and surgical time.

title: Advances in Musculoskeletal Imaging of the Foot and Ankle.
abstract: There have been many exciting advancements in imaging of the foot and ankle, particularly regarding the understanding of complex clinical conditions. Advances in imaging techniques, including high-resolution ultrasonography, multidetector CT, dual-energy CT, photon-counting CT, and MRI, have significantly enhanced the evaluation of the complex interplay of osseous and soft-tissue structure derangements in foot and ankle pathology. Ultrasonography provides dynamic assessment of tendon pathology; conventional CT offers detailed characterization of bone, tendon, and coalition. Dual-energy CT depicts bone marrow edema, photon-counting CT renders very high spatial resolution, and MRI remains the primary modality for evaluating tendon integrity, ligamentous injury, and bone marrow abnormalities with its superior soft-tissue contrast. Single-photon emission CT and metal artifact reduction sequence MRI have enhanced the evaluation of the painful total ankle arthroplasty, whereas weight-bearing CT has advanced the understanding of hallux valgus, trauma, and progressive collapsing foot deformity.

title: Scapula Fractures: Pearls and Pitfalls of Surgical Treatment.
abstract: Fractures of the scapula are rare, and they are frequently missed because of nonspecific symptoms, associated injuries, and limitations of standard radiographs. It is important to provide a comprehensive overview beginning with both common and uncommon presentations of scapular fractures and appropriate imaging modalities for both diagnosis and surgical planning. Key surgical indications should be outlined for glenoid, glenoid neck, and scapular body fractures, and floating shoulder, including discussion of the risks of inappropriately applied nonsurgical management. In addition, essential principles of surgical management, including timing, approach selection, and fixation strategies, as well as the importance of appropriate rehabilitation, are important topics of discussion. Practical guidance will help surgeons accurately diagnose and appropriately manage these challenging injuries to optimize patient outcomes.
